The Lions are coming off an overtime win against the Saints in a game where they led 21-0. Detroit is riddled with injuries in the secondary, including D.J. Reed and Brian Branch . That's terrible news against the Bills passing game. We're going to exploit that with two props. The first one is Josh Allen Over 249.5 Passing Yards . We just saw Allen torch an elite Texans defense for 334 yards through the air. It seems that now that Joe Brady is head coach instead of offensive coordinator, he is using his full authority to go more pass-heavy. In other words, it feels like Sean McDermott held back this offense. The Bills ranked second in Pass Rate Over Expected in Week 1, which supports this claim. With Allen airing it out more, set for a smash spot vs. the Lions, 250+ passing yards is firmly within reach. I'll finish it off with DJ Moore Over 62.5 Receiving Yards . We just saw Moore put up 100 yards in Week 1. He ranked third in air yards for the week at 160. Facing a weak Lions secondary, we should see Moore able to get to 63+ receiving yards here. The fact that this game is a projected shootout with a 54.5-point total makes me like these props even more, as it projects as the ideal game environment. To finish it off, we get the added narrative that this is the first game in a new stadium. It's going to be a raucous crowd, making it a tough environment for the Lions. Pictured: Josh Allen. It's Thursday Night Football, and Buffalo 's brand-new Highmark Stadium opens for business tonight, and it's opening with a shootout on deck. Both the Lions and the Bills arrive 1-0 after wild season openers, and Polymarket has priced up five separate contracts tied to tonight's game: everything from who wins outright down to how many times Josh Allen finds the end zone. Before locking anything in, check out our full Polymarket review , and download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis on tonight's card. If you're weighing your options on the platform, it's also worth looking up the current Polymarket promo code before kickoff. Thursday Night Football on Polymarket Traders buy and sell shares tied to a real outcome, and the price moves as new information comes in: injuries, weather, public opinion, whatever shifts the odds of that outcome happening. Tonight's game isn't limited to one contract, either. Beyond who wins, there are separate markets tracking the spread, the scoring total, the first half alone, and individual player output. Each one moves independently, which means the more interesting trades often sit outside the obvious who wins question. Lions vs. Bills: Spread This is the most heavily traded contract on the board. Buffalo is favored to win outright by a wider margin than this spread suggests. Both offenses looked dangerous in Week 1: Buffalo put up 36 on a Texans defense that had given Josh Allen trouble in each of the past two seasons, while Detroit needed overtime to put away New Orleans after its own defense let up 30. A near-even spread between two functioning offenses and two shaky defenses is exactly the kind of gap worth watching. Buffalo Moneyline Buffalo sits as the clear favorite here, but not by the margin the record and the home crowd might suggest. Detroit built a 21-0 lead over New Orleans in Week 1 and still needed overtime to close it out, watching that same defense let the Saints climb all the way back and force extra time. Its offense, with Goff, Gibbs , and Amon-Ra St. Brown , has traveled well before, but if the price on a Buffalo win doesn't account for how shaky Detroit's defense looked once that lead started slipping, that gap is worth a second look. Total Points: 54.5 These two offenses combined for 67 points in Week 1 against defenses that, on paper, aren't bad. Detroit 's unit gave up 30 in overtime, and Buffalo 's retooled defense under new coordinator Jim Leonhard hasn't faced an offense with this much speed yet. A stadium debut under the lights usually means fewer wrinkles and more of a team's base offense, which tends to push points up. That leans toward the Over here. First Half Total: 28.5 This number carries a fraction of the volume the full-game total does, which usually means the price hasn't fully caught up to what the bigger market already believes. If the shootout thesis behind the 54.5 line has any truth to it, an early scoring pace should show up well before the two-minute warning of the second quarter, not just late in the game. Josh Allen 2+ Touchdowns This is the one worth studying closest. Allen just posted two passing touchdowns and two rushing scores in Week 1 against a Texans defense that had shut him down in back-to-back meetings before that. Sometimes the ball bounces your way, Allen said after the win, and Buffalo's coaching staff will take four more bounces like that tonight. Yet the current price treats a repeat performance as unlikely. Detroit 's defense allowed 30 points in its own opener and hasn't faced a quarterback with Allen's legs yet this season. When a player's most recent outing and the market's price on him doing it again sit this far apart, that gap is usually worth digging into before it closes. Whatever combination catches your eye, keep in mind tonight's slate isn't one outcome dressed up five different ways. Each of these contracts reacts to its own set of information, and the interesting trades tend to live in the space between them. Lions vs Bills Spread Prediction Monday, Sept. 17 8:15 p.m. ET Prime Video Lions +5.5 (-102) By John Lanfranca The NFL began their early season Thursday night football slate in 2012. Since that point, underdogs of more than a field goal are 6-2 against the spread (ATS) in Week 2 on Thursday, specifically. Furthermore, in Week 2, all road underdogs have fared extremely well in recent years. Over the last five seasons, road teams playing as an underdog of more than a field goal are 24-11 against the number, covering at a 68.6% rate. This is only one data point that supports the Lions making Thursday Night Football a highly competitive game. The Bills defense has plenty of unanswered questions and I am not convinced they can consistently stop the run despite their performance against Houston in Week 1. Detroit had the highest rushing success rate league-wide a week ago against an improved Saints defense and should have the upper-hand once more against a Buffalo defense that ranked 30th in yards per carry in 2025. The Lions may have surrendered a league high in passing yards to Tyler Shough on Sunday, but their yards per attempt allowed still bested what Buffalo yielded to C.J. Stroud . The Lions were able to create pressure at a 40.6% rate. Only nine defensive units generated pressure at or above 40% in Week 1 and those teams went 9-0 straight up and 7-2 ATS. I expect Josh Allen to lead several scoring drives, but his reckless play combined with the Bills' aggressive approach with Joe Brady as head coach should give the Detroit defense some opportunities for takeaways. The Lions will turn any turnovers into points if they are gifted short fields. Don’t be surprised when this game goes down to the wire. I’d play the Lions down to +4 in what has historically been a very good week to back road underdogs. Pictured: Khalil Shakir. The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions kick off Thursday Night Football in Week 2 at the brand-new Highmark Stadium, with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET in the venue's regular-season debut. Both teams enter 1-0 after wild Week 1 wins, and with the total sitting at 54.5, the highest on this week's board, points are expected to come early and often. For more coverage of Thursday Night Football, check out Sean Koerner's Lions vs Bills preview. Tonight, I'm targeting Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid, Lions tight end Sam LaPorta, and Bills wide receiver Khalil Shakir to find the end zone first in the touchdown market. Continue below for my Lions vs Bills first touchdown props , and for more predictions and analysis for Thursday night football, download the Action Network app today. Lions vs Bills First Touchdown Props Dalton Kincaid First Touchdown (6% Yes, Kalshi ) Sam LaPorta First Touchdown (5% Yes, Kalshi) Khalil Shakir First Touchdown (5% Yes, Kalshi) Lions vs Bills Touchdown Scorer Picks Dalton Kincaid First Touchdown Dalton Kincaid looked every bit the X-factor Buffalo has waited three years for in Week 1. He hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 130 yards against Houston, including 35- and 40-yard gains, as new playcaller Joe Brady sent him downfield repeatedly with no linebacker or safety able to stay attached. That's the scheme detail that matters here. Brady isn't using Kincaid as a traditional in-line tight end running underneath routes — he's deploying him like a big slot receiver who wins vertically, and Josh Allen has already anointed him a stud this week. There's also a strong recency trend worth leaning on. Kincaid opened last season with a touchdown catch on Buffalo's very first scripted drive against Baltimore, and this Bills coaching staff has a track record of scripting an early shot to its most trusted mismatch. With Kincaid finally healthy after two seasons cut short by soft-tissue injuries, and Detroit's defense fresh off allowing 410 passing yards and three touchdowns to Tyler Shough and the Saints , the conditions are lined up for Allen to go back to the well early against a defense that just got shredded. Sam LaPorta First Touchdown Sam LaPorta 's resume speaks for itself. He's one of only three tight ends in NFL history, alongside Rob Gronkowski and Jimmy Graham, to reach 125 catches and 15 touchdowns through his first two seasons, and his 17 receiving touchdowns since entering the league are tied for the most at the position. Offensively, Ben Johnson may be gone to Chicago, but the scheme DNA he left behind with the Lions is still intact. Seam routes and option routes designed to put linebackers, not corners, on the ball remain central to how Detroit creates first-read touchdowns. LaPorta looked fully healthy in his return from offseason back surgery in Week 1, playing 81% of Detroit's snaps and catching 5-of-8 targets for 48 yards. Buffalo's defense will be locked in on stopping Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown , and Jameson Williams near the goal line. We've already seen Dalton Schultz , Marlin Klein, and Foster Moreau combine for 7 catches and 61 yards on a Bills defense preoccupied elsewhere last week. That's exactly the space LaPorta has historically feasted in, and Jared Goff trusts him enough in the red zone to make him a live first-score threat even in a game expected to feature 50-plus points. Khalil Shakir First Touchdown Khalil Shakir isn't the eye-catching name in this Bills offense anymore with DJ Moore aboard, but that's precisely what makes him a live long shot for the first score. Shakir is Allen's designed safety valve underneath while Moore and Kincaid occupy the defense over the top, and that role showed up immediately in Week 1 with four catches on six targets. The number that jumps out is his red-zone target share, which spiked to 25.5% last season, up from 14.8% the year before. Even as his overall volume stayed modest, it shows the coaching staff trusts him in scoring position regardless of who else is drawing targets elsewhere on the field. The matchup tilts things further in his favor. Detroit is missing both of its top safeties, Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, which thins out exactly the kind of underneath, over-the-middle coverage that normally limits a slot receiver like Shakir. Pictured: Joe Burrow. Our NFL Luck Rankings have proven to be a highly successful tool for betting NFL sides and totals. This year, we introduced Version 3.1 of our Luck Rankings as a way to continue to improve the methodology, as well as to simplify the thresholds and give you even better luck metrics. Continuing from Version 3.0 is something called the Luck Score . This single number will tell us whether a game has a significant luck factor. In Version 3.1, if the Luck Score is 1.9 or higher, we'll consider that a luck-based side. A 1.5-1.9 is considered a lean and won't count toward official Luck Rankings statistics. For totals, a Luck Total above +1.5 (over) or below -1.5 (under) is considered official for Luck Rankings record keeping, but as in years past this doesn't start until Week 3. Based on our Week 2 NFL Luck Rankings , there are two sides that are leans, and three totals that would have been official had it been Week 3 or later. Let's dive in. NFL Luck Rankings Week 2 Games Sides Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans Sunday, Sept .20 1 p.m. ET CBS Cincinnati was undoubtedly a bit fortunate to recover all four Tampa Bay fumbles in Week 1 — these types of plays are closer to 50/50 or 60/40 depending on who fumbles the ball, on what type of play, and where. Meanwhile, Houston lost a coin-flip game against Buffalo by five points, which is why my new Deserved Margins graph shows this as an effective tie based off our Expected Score metric (which power the Luck Rankings). If this game were last year, I'd be instantly betting the Texans , but the Bengals spent a ton of money in the offseason on improving their defense — it really showed in Week 1 as they forced four turnovers. Defensively, the Bengals only gave up 20 points (not counting the seven which came via a Joe Burrow pick-6), with three of those coming on a 58-yard field goal. That said, I still make Houston a field-goal favorite, leaning toward the 3.5. I don't see a reason to rush things here though, as the Luck Rankings have always graded against closing lines, and while leans aren't graded games, the theory would still apply. Since there has been no line movement this week on this game, and since I don't foresee any in the immediate future, I think it's fine to wait before backing the lean here. Verdict: Wait, lean Texans -2.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at New England Patriots Sunday, Sept. 20 1 p.m. ET CBS Drake Maye had a horrendous game against Seattle in a Super Bowl rematch, but certainly a shocking game like that is only a byproduct of New England being able to move the ball and still be in contention late. Maye's last interception came in the end zone on the last possession of the game, and all three of his interceptions came in the fourth quarter, with two occurring in Seahawks territory. Additionally, the Patriots struggled to run the ball against a Seattle defense that last year was the toughest in the league against the run, and clearly looks stout after one week this year as well. Pittsburgh should provide an easier task for the run game, and the Patriots are solid favorites here at home instead of on the road, so it's less likely Maye will have the errors that led to the Patriots' downfall in Week 1. I'm not betting a side here since it's just a lean at 54.7% LBC%, but I will have more to consider on this game below in the totals section. Verdict: Pass Totals The three games listed above all have totals that would be graded as Luck Rankings plays in Week 3 or later. Since it's not, these won't count toward official Luck Rankings records. With that said, of the three, I'm most inclined to lean toward the Cardinals /Seahawks game as the best of the three since I project this closer to 43 points even after accounting for the fact that Drew Lock is in at QB in place of Sam Darnold . That said, I want more time to evaluate this line, and I'm also not ready to buy in on a total with a backup QB, so I'm just going to pass on this one. One thing that's important to note is that the Patriots are an unlucky lean and the Luck Total in that game would be an over if it were Week 3 or later. That means we could consider looking at the Patriots to go over their team total. It's something I'll be eyeing as the week progresses. Pictured: Patrick Mahomes The first NFL week of the 2026 season is officially in the books! NFL Week 1 always feels like an early Christmas, with 16 games and 32 new presents of team data to unwrap and enjoy. There's nothing quite like the time-honored tradition of overreacting to everything we saw on opening week, so let's overreact to one thing each from all 16 games, then reach an early verdict on whether that overreaction is a real or not real takeaway from Week 1. Along the way, we'll add to our futures portfolio with six new bets. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! NFL Week 1 Overreactions » NAVIGATION « DEN vs KC | NE vs SEA | SF vs LAR | ARI vs LAC | WAS vs PHI | DAL vs NYG | BAL vs IND | CLE vs JAX BUF vs HOU | GB vs MIN | CHI vs CAR | NO vs DET | TB vs CIN | NYJ vs TEN | ATL vs PIT | MIA vs LV Click here to return to the table of contents. Chiefs 31, Broncos 10 Overreaction: Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs are back!! Kansas City absolutely crushed Denver. The Broncos won 15 games last year, ran it back, and everyone drafted them as a unanimous top-five team. That never made sense to me. The Chiefs are the real top-five team, and Denver is in big trouble with a possibly fraudulent defense and Davis Webb’s offense. This wasn't even a Patrick Mahomes masterclass — the Chiefs just dominated the trenches and unveiled an entirely new offense. They ran Duo, stayed under center, and let Kenneth Walker explode for 173 yards and two touchdowns. Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith completely overwhelmed a supposedly elite Broncos run defense. The Chiefs doubled up Denver's yardage, averaging almost six yards per play while holding Bo Nix to four sacks, three fumbles, and an embarrassingly low aDOT. I am buying Creed Humphrey for Protector of the Year at 3% on Kalshi to add to my awards portfolio. Verdict: REAL Click here to return to the table of contents. Seahawks 13, Patriots 10 Overreaction: Regression is already coming hard for both Super Bowl teams!! This was a rusty, ugly, slow Week 1 game that felt a lot like their Super Bowl matchup. Seattle basically had no offense until 18 minutes were left, and New England would have won if Drake Maye didn't throw three bad interceptions — including a back-breaker with 21 seconds left in field-goal range. But sometimes regression simply means injuries. Sam Darnold 's hip injury is an unknown, but Drew Lock is generally around the 35th-to-40th best quarterback by PFF grade, which makes him a perfectly capable backup. Darnold is only around QB20 anyway, so it's not a massive downgrade on paper. Seattle's schedule also lines up perfectly to weather the storm with Arizona and Washington up next. A.J. Brown 's injury for New England is far more meaningful. With Brown out, Kayshon Boutte traded and Romeo Doubs MIA, the Patriots drop from a top-eight to bottom-eight receiving corps. That takes them from a fringe top-10 offense to league average, shifting them a full point against the spread. Maye struggled to pass deep, and the rushing attack was awful (-0.45 EPA/play on a 22% success rate ). New England plays Pittsburgh, Jacksonville, and Buffalo next. The Patriots are already behind the eight ball and could easily start 1-3. Verdict: REAL for New England, NOT REAL yet for Seattle Click here to return to the table of contents. 49ers 27, Rams 7 Overreaction: The Rams' dream season is already in huge trouble!! The 49ers dominated this game from start to finish with a massive 57% to 43% edge in success rate. They should be No. 1 in any power rankings after doing that to the consensus top team. But the real story was Myles Garrett , who recorded zero tackles, zero pressures, and zero sacks — and now we know why. Garrett heading to IR means he misses at least the next four games against the Giants , Broncos , Eagles , and Bills . That is an enormous downgrade. A team that relies heavily on its edge rush now has a glaring weakness with Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart trying to fill the void. This technically counts as a home division loss for the Rams , and the rest of the division is already 1-0. If they drop a few of these upcoming games against top-tier offensive lines without Garrett, they might lose the division and be forced to play road playoff games instead of staying at SoFi. FTN currently projects the Rams at 9.6 wins — well under their 11.5 total. The dream season is already in some serious jeopardy. Verdict: VERY REAL Click here to return to the table of contents. Cardinals 26, Chargers 14 Overreaction: The Chargers might’ve already Chargers’d their season away!! This wasn't fluky at all. The Cardinals put up almost 400 yards and outgained Los Angeles by 125 yards. The Chargers offense looked good until Ladd McConkey got hurt (8.9 YPA passing with him, 3.9 YPA without him). The injury exposed their lack of depth at receiver, and the interior offensive line struggled mightily. This is a terrible loss for the Chargers. This was supposed to be the easiest game on a really tough schedule, so we have to downgrade them by almost a full win on their season projection. Mike McDaniel's offense is going to take time. FTN projects the Bolts for 7.4 wins and just a 29% chance to make the playoffs, which is even lower than the Jets and Giants. I am betting the Chargers to miss the playoffs at -120 on BetMGM . How about a second crazy bet? I'm putting a 0.25-unit nibble on the Cardinals to win the NFC West at +12500 (Caesars) . Myles Garrett and Sam Darnold are already hurt in that division, and Arizona plays Seattle with Drew Lock this week. No 1-0 NFL team should ever be priced at 125-1 to win their division. Verdict: REAL Click here to return to the table of contents. Eagles 24, Commanders 22 Overreaction: The Eagles' offense is STILL broken!! The Commanders were probably the better team here. Jayden Daniels passed the eye test, and Daronte Jones called a great game defensively with a high blitz rate that made Philadelphia uncomfortable. The Eagles won, but it was ugly. They had four scoring drives, and each one relied entirely on a single explosive play (a 46-yard Saquon Barkley run, and passes of 31, 43, and 64 yards). Outside of those four plays, Philly tallied just 99 yards on 50 plays. That's under two yards per play with an abysmal 34% success rate, including a 3rd-percentile 28% success rate on early downs. Jalen Hurts had zero designed runs. Barkley rushed 15 times for 41 yards outside of his one explosive burst. The Sean Mannion offense looks broken, and now Landon Dickerson — their best interior lineman — is heading to IR as Philly's rushing metrics continue to struggle. Philadelphia was lucky to pull out a win here. I already bet Under 40.5 in their matchup against the Titans next week. Verdict: REAL Click here to return to the table of contents. Giants 28, Cowboys 20 Overreaction: Giants Island, worst-to-first 2026!! Giants Island looks like the real deal, and this is exactly how we drew it up. John Harbaugh brought over his older Ravens personnel —Patrick Ricard at fullback, Isaiah Likely at tight end — and ran a smash-mouth, ball-control offense. The Giants converted 9-of-11 third downs, outgained Dallas by 150 yards, and lived in the 99th percentile for success rate while staying ahead of the chains. Jaxson Dart looked steady and in control, making good decisions. After halftime, the Giants orchestrated touchdown drives of 8:01 and 8:11 minutes to completely kill off the clock. Dallas actually scored touchdowns on all of its second-half possessions — but it only had two! The Cowboys offense looks fine, but the defense got completely shredded and pushed around by a very basic game plan. This Giants formula — run the ball, limit possessions, hit a few explosives — looks replicable. Verdict: REAL Click here to return to the table of contents. </a

(Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images) It's that time of year when hope springs anew and the NFL-loving public collectively says, This year, I'll go all the way. I'm of course referring to NFL survivor pools, a type of contest that sounds easy — until you're doing it. That brings us to our NFL Survivor Pool Week 2 picks. The concept is simple: Pick one team that wins an NFL game every week. No spreads or totals, just winners. Once you use that team, they're done — creating an element of strategy and long-term planning that makes these contests deceptively difficult. Fortunately, we've continued our partnership with our friends at PoolGenius to make things easier. They've built slate-leading tools to help conquer a variety of pool contests, including survivor. My favorite feature of the site is the ability to customize for your individual pool type. Factors like contest size and payout structure are huge in survivor contests, as smaller fields generally don't have any entries that make it all 18 weeks. To give a glimpse of how that works, throughout the season, I'll be providing their top option for small (less than 100) and large (1,000+) entry pools. I'm also including an alternate/contrarian option for those of us playing multiple entries in a single pool, as a means of diversifying. Besides that, they track pick selection data to help figure out contrarian options. This is helpful in larger pools since we're trying to optimize for expected value more than just odds of winning. Finally, they use projected future spreads to assign a future value to each team — which includes considering the scarcity of strong options on certain weeks. This is crucial, as we don't want to burn the best teams when there are other strong options that week. To get their full data, you'll need to sign up for the site. It's well worth it, though, and it also includes tools for taking down the increasingly popular pick'em contests that feature massive prize pools. NFL Survivor Pool Picks Get Survivor Picks Now NFL Survivor Picks from PoolGenius Season Discounts via Action Network Small Field: Tampa Bay Bucs My personal favorite pick this week is the Buccaneers , who are projecting as the second-most utilized team and have the third-best moneyline odds on the slate. Second-most utilized is a bit misleading as PoolGenius has the top two teams basically even, but Tampa just slightly below. The reason I prefer the Bucs at -400 or so odds to teams more likely to win is their lack of future value. At no other point this season is Tampa Bay projected to even be a -200 favorite — though that can obviously change — so it is close to a now-or-never team. Obviously with pools larger than 100 or so entrants we expect to need to last all 18 weeks, so using the Bucs now preserves stronger teams for late in the season when we're likely to need them. Assuming they win, you'd feel pretty good with an entry that started with the Bucs and Raiders , for example, competing against entries that have already burned stronger teams. Small Field: San Francisco 49ers Currently, PoolGenius is projecting the 49ers to be the most popular team on the slate, but with a relatively even split between San Francisco and Tampa Bay. We had a similar dynamic last week with the Jaguars and the Chargers , where Los Angeles was the chalk play in theory. That turned out to not be the case in sharper pools, where a decent chunk of the field pivoted to the Jaguars in order to avoid the chalk — but that made the Jaguars more popular in some contests. I wouldn't be shocked if we had a similar scenario here with the field leveling itself off on the 49ers, despite their massive -900 or so moneyline as they host the Dolphins . That level of safety is worth sacrificing some future value for, especially in pools we don't expect to make it all 18 weeks. One of the better future spots for the 49ers is a Week 18 matchup with the Cardinals , which obviously isn't relevant if your pool wraps up in Week 17 or earlier. I'm a bit nervous about the 49ers given the travel back from Australia, but they have four extra days of rest and looked great in that game against the Rams. Plus, the betting market seems to have no such concern, so I'll trust the odds in some of my contests. Contrarian Option: Chicago Bears I will be diversifying a bit with the Bears , who are projecting for virtually no utilization by the field (about 2%). They have a somewhat challenging divisional matchup against the Vikings this week, but this is their home game against Minnesota, and Chicago is about 70% implied to win. Chicago has some other decent spots later in the season, but I've played with PoolGenius's season planner a bit this week and don't really find myself missing the Bears much when I burn them this week, and they're a massive leverage option. Not only would you gain a ton of equity if San Francisco or Tampa Bay were to be upset, but you'd be able to be contrarian again in later weeks by keeping those teams available. The 49ers, in particular, have some other solid spots, and over the course of the season more could emerge for Tampa Bay as well. As always, this isn't a pick I'd make if playing just one entry this year, but if you're playing multiple pools it makes a lot of sense to diversify and give yourself a potential hedge in case of a big upset to one of the top teams. Let us take a look at who is currently in the crosshairs. The Fired Coaches Odds: The Sirianni Case The Kalshi board features a clear frontrunner to be out of a job before March 2027: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni , who commands a 72% implied probability. He is followed on the board by Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers at 53%, while Dan Quinn , currently at the helm of the Washington Commanders, holds a 50% chance of losing his job in the coming months. What makes the Nick Sirianni situation so intriguing is that the Kalshi board appears to reflect an overly negative sentiment regarding his future. The Philadelphia Eagles won their season opener against Quinn's Commanders, and while their execution was far from flawless, the victory certainly quelled any immediate doubts about Sirianni's job security. However, this market prices in the long grind from the regular season to the Super Bowl, and a lot can happen in the coming months. Against that backdrop, the Eagles face several hurdles that Sirianni must clear if he wants to extend his stay in Philadelphia. First and foremost are injuries and the need to establish a cohesive starting lineup. For instance, despite being listed as available against the Commanders, wide receiver Hollywood Brown did not play a single snap. Sirianni took accountability for his absence on behalf of the coaching staff: We obviously want to get him into the football game because his speed is real. It just didn't work out that way yesterday. There are games like that. There are games where you get shut out on catches, Sirianni said. What About Matt LaFleur? On one hand, the Kalshi market appears to be overpricing Sirianni's vulnerability while simultaneously underestimating the heat under Matt LaFleur's seat in Green Bay. The main catalyst fueling doubts around LaFleur's future was the Packers' abysmal Week 1 performance against the Vikings. Green Bay once again struggled to close out a game, and their second-half collapse exposed deeper issues, not just with the roster's ability to execute under pressure, but with LaFleur's game management and underwhelming tactical adjustments. Carrying a 22-17 lead into the fourth quarter, the Packers completely unraveled down the stretch against Minnesota. Even after losing their starting quarterback early in the contest, the Vikings turned to backup Carson Wentz and stormed away with a 39-22 victory. Looking ahead at the Packers' upcoming schedule, it is definitely not an easy stretch, which severely limits Matt LaFleur's margin for error following their Week 1 division loss to Minnesota. If front office pressure builds, the upcoming Month 1 and Month 2 slate features crucial trap games and brutal division matchups that will determine LaFleur's job security. What Moves the Odds? When analyzing these markets, it is crucial to remember that a win-loss record is far from the only variable putting a head coach on the hot seat. Preseason expectations, trader projections, and total franchise investment can either magnify or soften the blow of early losses. A team in full rebuild mode with a crowded injury report does not enter the season expecting to contend for a Super Bowl. In those scenarios, both the front office and fanbase are generally far more patient with the head coach as they work toward long-term stability. Conversely, a perennial contender stacked with top-tier talent will face intense scrutiny if the wins fail to materialize. Additionally, keep in mind that a newly appointed GM or owner almost always wants to bring in their own guy. If a head coach was inherited by a new front-office regime, their implied firing odds carry an inherent market premium compared to coaches who are fully aligned with their general manager. Pictured: Patrick Mahomes. Five prediction markets are moving for very different reasons this week on Kalshi : an election, a movie reboot, and NFL and MLB games. Chiefs vs Colts The Colts travel to Arrowhead Stadium for Sunday Night Football in a game that doubles as a return-to-health story for both starting quarterbacks: Patrick Mahomes is back from a torn ACL, and Daniel Jones is back from a torn Achilles. Kansas City also added reigning Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III to its backfield this offseason, and the market already has Kansas City as a clear favorite over an Indianapolis team looking to bounce back from a rough Week 1 loss. Why It's Worth Trading This Week: Two starting quarterbacks are getting their first real test since major injuries, in primetime, against playoff-caliber pass rushes. Our take: We're leaning toward the Chiefs here. Mahomes at home, with a healthier backfield than a year ago, is a tough matchup for a Colts defense that just gave up 41 points in Week 1: injury questions aside, the supporting cast gap favors the Chiefs. Brazil's Presidential Race Flips on Kalshi For the first time since polling began, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is trading ahead of President Lula da Silva on Kalshi's Brazil presidential election winner contract. Bolsonaro , running with his imprisoned father's public blessing, has climbed as September surveys from pollsters like AtlasIntel show him edging into the lead for a potential runoff. Lula , seeking a fourth term at 80, still leads most first-round numbers, so the flip says more about runoff math than about the October 4 vote itself. Why It's Worth Trading This Week: The first round lands in three weeks, and every new poll is repricing the contract in real time. The next data drop could move things again before Sunday. Resident Evil Rotten Tomatoes Score Zach Cregger's Resident Evil reboot releases on September 18, so this is the week critic reviews start counting. Kalshi's own forecast for the eventual score is about 81 now , even though Cregger's last two films, Barbarian and Weapons , both landed in the low-to-mid 90s on Rotten Tomatoes . Why It's Worth Trading This Week: Video game adaptations rarely clear the bar horror directors do, and this is Cregger's first time working inside someone else's universe instead of an original script. That gap between his track record and the genre's history is exactly what makes the score worth a position before the embargo lifts. Our Take: We'd lean toward the 80-85 range . Cregger's talents are real, but adapting an established franchise usually costs a few points against an original idea: strong reviews, not necessarily a clean sweep. The Northern Ireland Question This contract tracks whether the UK 's Secretary of State for Northern Ireland formally calls a border poll on Irish reunification before Jan 1, 2030. It traded quietly for months until President Donald Trump told reporters in Dublin over the weekend he'd love to see a united Ireland eventually. Why It's Worth Trading This Week: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called a referendum off the table for now. Expect renewed volume as UK officials keep responding through the week. Our Take: It's certainly something to monitor, but we're leaning toward no for now. While this is something that multiple parties would like to see, the valuable play is to hold off. The reason for this being 'off the table' is because the Northern Ireland people aren't asking for it. Polls seem to indicate that the Northern Ireland people prefer to stay in the United Kingdom. Fed Decision This Week The Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday and Wednesday, and Kalshi's September decision contract has swung hard toward a quarter-point increase after August's hotter-than-expected inflation report. A hold was the favored outcome three weeks ago; that flipped after Chair Kevin Warsh 's Jackson Hole remarks and this month's CPI print. Why It's Worth Trading This Week: Wednesday's announcement is the resolution. The contract has swung by dozens of points twice in the past month, so there's no guarantee the current lean holds until then. How Prediction Markets Work Each of these markets works the same way: a contract priced between 1¢ and 99¢, where the price reflects the market's live estimate of that outcome's probability. Traders can buy a yes or no position and hold it to resolution, or sell early if the price moves in their favor. Unlike a fixed line, the price updates continuously as new information comes in: a poll, a review, a box score, which is why each of the five contracts above has already moved more than once this week. Pictured: Tyler Shough. New Orleans' real conviction behind Tyler Shough nearly paid off with a win in Week 1, but we saw why the team is keen on his future. By throwing for 410 yards against a mighty Detroit Lions team, Shough was the engine that had New Orleans remembering what it was like to have Drew Brees under center. The Saints are 0-1, but they walked away with a stock-up designation after their Week 1 performance. New Orleans Saints Season Odds The odds widgets throughout this preview track how the Saints are priced across division, playoff, conference and player markets in real time; here's what tends to move those numbers on Polymarket . New Orleans's division and playoff pricing reflects a team the market takes more seriously than its 6-11 record from a year ago would suggest, since that record obscures a genuine second-half turnaround under a since-established starting quarterback. Traders tend to weight a team's most recent form more heavily than its full-season record once a clear inflection point, like a midseason quarterback change, explains most of the gap between the two. Continuity at coach and both coordinators works in New Orleans's favor here, since a full season together removes one of the bigger variables that usually caps a team's pricing after a rebuilding year. The division itself remains unusually open, with four teams bunched closely enough that no single result likely settles the race before midseason. Conference and Super Bowl futures for a team like this move slowly and stay modest until a full season of results confirms whether the late-2025 surge was real progress or a soft closing schedule. Market participants generally wait for head-to-head divisional results before fully repricing a team coming off a losing record. New Orleans sits second in a genuinely open NFC South, trailing only Tampa Bay and priced well ahead of both Carolina, the defending division champion, and Atlanta, a sign the market has bought into the second-half turnaround more than the win total alone would justify. Top New Orleans Saints Team Prop Contracts Team stat-leader contracts for a team with a newly established starting quarterback carry real uncertainty, since a full offseason of game-planning around him is different from the half-season sample the market has to work with. A passing offense that improved sharply once a new starter took over doesn't automatically carry that improvement into a full 17-game season. That uncertainty tends to keep a team's stat-leader pricing tied more closely to its clearest individual strength than to a fully proven system, at least early on. A featured back or an established No. 1 receiver gives a team a stat-leader floor that the rest of the offense hasn't yet earned on a full-season sample. Traders following these markets for New Orleans should watch early rushing volume and target share closely, since those numbers will show whether the second-half identity from 2025 carries over or whether a full season of preparation from opposing defenses changes the picture. New Orleans's 2025 offense ranked 22nd in total yards and 28th in scoring across the full season, numbers dragged down by a rough start that Shough's second-half performance doesn't fully erase in the year-end totals. Top New Orleans Saints Player Prop Contracts Player-level contracts for a quarterback with a genuine but small sample size price differently than they do for a fully proven starter, since the market has to weigh a strong half-season against the possibility that opposing defenses adjust once they have a full offseason of tape. A passer's tiered yardage and touchdown markets tend to reflect that caution directly in how quickly the pricing thins out at higher tiers. Award markets like MVP work against a team coming off a losing record almost entirely, regardless of individual promise, since MVP pricing requires team success layered on top of strong play. A running back or quarterback putting up real production on a team that missed the playoffs typically doesn't crack the field's leading names. Traders reassess New Orleans's player markets constantly through camp and the preseason, watching how a full year of continuity at coordinator translates individual usage into results, since that's the clearest early signal of whether last year's second-half surge was sustainable. Shough's passing-yardage market and Etienne's rushing-yardage market both show real conviction at the lower tiers, with Etienne in particular priced as a strong favorite to clear a solid rushing floor behind an offensive line the team specifically retooled this offseason. Confidence in both fades at the tiers that would represent a genuine breakout season, consistent with the caution the market is showing across New Orleans's other markets. new_body: Panthers vs. Falcons (Sep 20, 2026) Pregame - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Carolina Panthers @ Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers Panthers CAR 0-1 , 0-0 Away FOX Atlanta Falcons Falcons ATL 0-1 , 0-0 Home By AP Updated: Sep 17, 2026, 03:55 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email ATLANTA -- — The NFC South suffered the indignity of having four teams finish with losing records last season and take Week 1 losses to open the 2026 season. Last week's poor showing makes division matchups, including Carolina's visit to Atlanta on Sunday, especially important. Though the Panthers finished with the same 8-9 regular-season record as Atlanta and Tampa Bay last season, they swept the two games against the Falcons on their way to winning the division title tiebreaker. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young says coach Dave Canales has stressed that the best route to the playoffs is winning in the division. “Coach talks about it all of the time," Young said. ”Our first goal is to win the South. Obviously those division wins mean so much when you’re trying to accomplish that goal. You have the same process for every game — you don’t get too high or too low, but this is a business and we are all players and we understand what is at stake every time there is a division opponent. We know what this game means.” Atlanta's home opener follows a 20-13 opening loss at Pittsburgh last week. The Falcons were forced to start third-string quarterback Cooper Rush after Tua Tagovailoa suffered an oblique injury in practice and Michael Penix Jr . continued his recovery from a 2025 season-ending left knee injury. Rush threw two interceptions, including T.J. Watt’s pick-6 in the fourth quarter. Despite continued uncertainty at quarterback this week, the Falcons' bigger problem may be finding a way to contain Young and the Panthers' passing game. Young set a franchise record by passing for 448 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in Carolina's 30-27 overtime win at Atlanta to sweep the Falcons last season. “He’s a very smart quarterback,” said Falcons safety Jessie Bates III of Young. "I think they’ve done a lot of really good things to help him bring out his strengths in his game, whether that’s them going to empty or rhythm-type of throws to help them out. I think that he’s definitely become a really high-level quarterback in this league for sure.” Young's top playmakers are Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , an undrafted rookie in 2024 who had eight catches for a career-high 138 yards and two touchdowns in last week's 59-37 loss to Chicago. Need to know Carolina (0-1) at Atlanta (0-1) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox Latest odds: Panthers by 2 1/2. Against the spread: Panthers 0-1; Falcons 0-1. Last week: Panthers lost Bears 59-37; Falcons lost to Steelers 20-13. Last meeting: Panthers beat Falcons 30-27 in overtime in Atlanta on Nov. 16, 2025. Series record: Falcons lead 37-25. Matchup to watch Panthers run defense vs. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson . The Panthers allowed two Chicago running backs to reach 100 rushing yards in the Bears' 59-37 win last week in Charlotte. Overall, the Bears rushed for 291 yards and six touchdowns and averaged 7.5 yards per carry. Robinson had 21 carries for 83 yards and eight receptions for 90 yards in the Falcons' 20-13 loss at Pittsburgh as the focal point of an offense that had a limited passing game. Stats and stuff — The Panthers and Bears combined to score 96 points in Week 1, making it the highest-scoring season-opening game in NFL history. Unfortunately for the Panthers, they gave up 59 of those points, the most in franchise history. — Panthers WR Jalen Coker had eight catches for a career-high 138 yards and two touchdowns in the Week 1 shootout with the Bears. — RB Chuba Hubbard had a touchdown rushing and a touchdown receiving in Week 1 and remains the Panthers top option in the backfield. — The Panthers defense allowed six touchdowns rushing against the Bears and two TDs in each quarter. — Young is 4-1 against the Falcons, completing 110 of 165 pass attempts (66.7%) for 1,133 yards and seven touchdowns. He is 10-30 as a starter against the rest of the league. — With Rush at quarterback, Drake London had only two catches for 29 yards and Kyle Pitts had no catches and only one target against Pittsburgh. London, Atlanta’s go-to wide receiver and Pitts, coming off a productive season at tight end, each received new contracts in the offseason. — Tagovailoa did not participate in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Cornerback A.J. Terrell (shoulder) was a full participant on Thursday after being held out Wednesday. RG Chris Lindstrom (concussion protocol) was limited on Thursday after being held out Wednesday. — The Falcons are 21-10 at home in the rivalry. — The Falcons ranked 31st in passing yards and 30th in total yards following their weak offensive showing in their opener. ------ AP Sports Writer Steve Reed in Charlotte, N.C., contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here Terms of Use Privacy Policy Your US State Privacy Rights Children's Online Privacy Policy Interest-Based Ads About Nielsen Measurement Your Privacy Choices Contact Us Disney Ad Sales Site Work for ESPN Corrections GAMBLING PROBLEM? Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Finebaum: Pressure is all on Lane Kiffin in LSU-Ole Miss showdown (1:42) ESPN News Services Multiple Authors Sep 17, 2026, 03:03 PM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright are ineligible to join any NFL teams this season after they attempted to return to college and play for LSU , the league said in a memo sent to each NFL team Wednesday. Harris was a defensive tackle and Wright played tight end for Ole Miss during its run to a College Football Playoff semifinal last season. Both signed contracts in the NFL this summer after going undrafted. They then tried joining former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin at LSU and sued for the right to regain their college eligibility. Wright's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told Front Office Sports that "Dae'Quan is looking at his legal options right now and we will have more to say in the near future." The NFL Players Association, meanwhile, told Front Office Sports that it was "in touch with each of the players' representatives. "We will explore all options to ensure each players' rights are protected within the Collective Bargaining Agreement." After the Southeastern Conference passed a rule barring pros from heading back to college to play and a Louisiana court put that restriction on hold, LSU left both players off its roster as it opened its season. The NFL's letter noted that both Harris and Wright "were eligible for the 2026 NFL Draft, returned to college and participated with their college football team after the opening of NFL training camp, and therefore, they are ineligible to visit, try out with or be signed by NFL clubs during the 2026 season." Harris and Wright were the only players mentioned in the letter. The NFL acknowledged this list didn't include all 2026 draft-eligible players who returned to college and said teams should contact the league's player personnel department with any questions about a player's eligibility. The letter also noted that it is each team's responsibility to verify a player's eligibility. Discipline for eligibility violations can include fines and/or the loss of draft picks. The NFL had informed its teams in late August that any player who returned to the college ranks would be prohibited from signing with an NFL team this season. It said any player cut by an NFL team who returned to college this year would be considered a free agent and therefore not subject to a future draft. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

new_body: Vikings vs. Bears (Sep 20, 2026) Pregame - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Minnesota Vikings @ Chicago Bears Minnesota Vikings Vikings MIN 1-0 , 0-0 Away FOX Chicago Bears Bears CHI 1-0 , 0-0 Home By AP Sep 17, 2026, 02:31 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email CHICAGO -- — It's a stressful week for Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson. Same for Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. They have that type of effect on each other. Johnson and Flores match wits once again on Sunday when Caleb Williams and Chicago host Dallas Turner and Minnesota for their home opener. Johnson is 5-1 when calling the plays against a Flores-coached defense, averaging 27.5 points per game. “When you go against a guy like this, you’ve got everything,” Johnson said. “So that’s where it’s a lot. For our players, they have to really dedicate themselves over the course of the week to have success on game day and fortunately I do think our guys, the way we train them is very demanding and very detailed with teams like this in mind.” Flores, 45, is known for his array of blitzes, and he really turned up the pressure in the final part of Minnesota's 39-22 win over Green Bay in Week 1. The Vikings trailed 22-10 in the third quarter, but they sacked Jordan Love four times in the second half. Love also lost a fumble and threw an interception in the fourth quarter. Turner was credited with a career-high seven QB hits, the most in an NFL game since Chris Jones had eight for Kansas City in Week 15 of the 2018 season. “You’d like to think he’s put everything he could possibly do on tape until you play him next and you realize he hasn’t yet,” Johnson said. “So it’ll be something new. There always is with him and that’s what makes him such a good coordinator. It’s a great challenge. It really is.” Johnson, 40, also presents quite the challenge for Flores and Minnesota's defense. Chicago totaled 291 yards rushing and 552 yards overall in its 59-37 victory at Carolina on Sunday. It was the highest-scoring season opener in NFL history. “What are we getting week to week? It’s hard to know,” Flores said. “So a lot of the game is adjustments. If they do this, we want to do that. If they do that, we want to do this. And we’re going to have our own game plan to start things off. It’s the same thing on his end: What are they doing? And how are we going to counteract what they’re doing? So it’s certainly a chess match.” Williams passed for two touchdowns and rushed for two more TDs in the first game of his second season in Johnson’s offense. The 24-year-old quarterback definitely has the Vikings' attention. “He’s obviously capable of making highlight play after highlight play," Vikings safety Harrison Smith said. "He’s really got it all. He’s extremely talented. He’s operating that offense very well.” Need to know Minnesota (1-0) at Chicago (1-0). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox. Latest odds: Bears by 4 1/2. Against the spread: Vikings 1-0; Bears 1-0. Last week: Vikings beat the Packers 39-22; Bears beat the Panthers 59-37. Last meeting: Bears beat Vikings 19-17 on Nov. 16 in Minnesota. Series record: Vikings lead 69-59-2. Matchup to watch Vikings WR Justin Jefferson vs Bears CB Jaylon Johnson . Jefferson, 27, and Johnson, 27, know each other quite well. They are both 2020 draft picks who have spent their entire careers with their respective NFC North teams. Jefferson had eight catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Minnesota's season opener. He has 59 receptions for 790 yards and four TDs in 10 games against Chicago. Johnson is looking to bounce back from a shaky performance at Carolina. He missed both of Chicago's games against Minnesota last season. He has one interception in six games versus the Vikings. Stats and stuff — The Vikings have won six straight games at Soldier Field, one short of the franchise record for consecutive road wins over a division opponent. They won seven straight at Detroit from 1968-74 and seven straight on the road against Green Bay from 1971-77. — In Week 1, the Vikings became the first team in NFL history to win by 17 or more points after trailing by 12 or more points with less than 20 minutes left in regulation, according to Stats Perform . — Bears running back D’Andre Swift is 101 yards shy of 5,000 yards rushing for his career. The 27-year-old Swift rushed for 124 yards and three touchdowns in Week 1. — Bears tight end Cole Kmet needs four receptions to pass Allen Robinson (293) for ninth on the franchise's career list. Kmet had two catches for 35 yards and a TD against the Panthers. ------ AP Pro Football Writer Dave Campbell contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here Terms of Use Privacy Policy Your US State Privacy Rights Children's Online Privacy Policy Interest-Based Ads About Nielsen Measurement Your Privacy Choices Contact Us Disney Ad Sales Site Work for ESPN Corrections GAMBLING PROBLEM? new_body: Eagles vs. Titans (Sep 20, 2026) Pregame - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Philadelphia Eagles @ Tennessee Titans Philadelphia Eagles Eagles PHI 1-0 , 0-0 Away FOX Tennessee Titans Titans TEN 0-1 , 0-1 Home By AP Sep 17, 2026, 01:01 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- — Coach Nick Sirianni wants his Philadelphia Eagles to remember just how hard winning in the NFL really is and take time to enjoy each victory. “It’s so important that joy comes after every time,” Sirianni said. “I already know how I’m going to feel if we lose. That is a feeling that’s hard to get over. You better appreciate the things and know how hard it is and appreciate those things after a win.” The Eagles have won a lot with Sirianni, reaching the playoffs in each of his first five seasons and going 1-1 in the Super Bowl. They just opened his sixth season with a 24-22 win over Washington that might not garner any style points. Still, the Eagles improved to 6-0 in season openers with Sirianni. Now Philadelphia visits the struggling Tennessee Titans (0-1) on Sunday to kick off a two-game road swing. Oh yeah, the Eagles also have the NFL's best road winning percentage at .698 (30-13) since 2021, and they're 10-3 in that span against AFC teams. The Eagles have to figure out who replaces three-time Pro Bowl left guard Landon Dickerson , who went on injured reserve Tuesday with an injured knee. Sirianni likes Philadelphia's options behind the veteran, but not having Dickerson will be different. “There haven’t been many games that I’ve been the head coach here that he wasn’t playing football for us,” Sirianni said of Dickerson. “Obviously, going to miss him like crazy, but really excited about that room and the depth of that room and where we are there.” Tennessee opened the 28th and final season at Nissan Stadium with a 23-10 loss to the New York Jets . The Titans were dominated across the board in that game with issues new coach Robert Saleh says are correctable. Right tackle JC Latham called the loss humbling and a reality check: "We know what our identity is, and that wasn't it." The loss appeared to be Tennessee finding new ways to lose with new coaches and players after a string of four miserable seasons . The Titans not only hired Saleh as a new coach, they also spent heavily in free agency trying to add talent to a young roster. Saleh said their goal Sunday isn't to prove anyone wrong. “It’s just prove that we can get better, prove that we can compete and prove that we’re a team that’s capable of stringing together four quarters and win football games,” Saleh said. Need to know Philadelphia (1-0) at Tennessee (0-1) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox Latest odds: Eagles by 7. Against the spread: Eagles 0-1, Titans 0-1. Last game: Eagles beat Washington 24-22, and the Titans lost 23-10 to the Jets. Last meeting: Eagles beat the Titans 35-10 on Dec. 4, 2022, in Philadelphia. Series record: Eagles lead 8-5. Matchup to watch The Titans run defense against Eagles running back Saquon Barkley and quarterback Jalen Hurts . Tennessee spent heavily adding linemen John Franklin -Myers, Jermaine Johnson II and Jacob Martin to the roster. The Titans gave up 152 yards rushing on 39 attempts to the Jets, including 10 straight run plays in a 19-play drive. Barkley and Hurts combined for 129 rushing yards. Stats and stuff — The Eagles are visiting Nashville for only the fourth time since the Titans moved into Nissan Stadium in 1999. — The Eagles are 14-4 in September since the start of the 2021 season. — The home team has won five of the past six in this sporadic series. — The Titans are hosting back-to-back games to open a season for the first time since 2010. — Eagles QB Jalen Hurts threw for 203 yards and three touchdowns last week. — Eagles WR Dontayvion Wicks had two catches for 73 yards and a TD in the opener. — TE Dallas Goedert led the Eagles with 77 yards receiving and two TDs last week. — Titans LB Anthony Hill tied for the NFL lead with 16 tackles in Week 1, the most by a rookie in his debut since 2000. Hill also defended two passes. — Titans QB Cam Ward threw for 140 yards and a TD last week. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here Terms of Use Privacy Policy Your US State Privacy Rights Children's Online Privacy Policy Interest-Based Ads About Nielsen Measurement Your Privacy Choices Contact Us Disney Ad Sales Site Work for ESPN Corrections GAMBLING PROBLEM? Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Bryce Young previews divisional showdown with Falcons (0:47) Mike Kaye Sep 17, 2026, 06:00 AM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions During the third quarter of a back-and-forth divisional donnybrook to end the 2024 season, the Carolina Panthers trailed the Atlanta Falcons by one point, roughly four minutes into the second half. It was fourth-and-1 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Bryce Young lined up under center and took a snap before faking a handoff to running back Miles Sanders . With tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders darting to the right behind the line of scrimmage to pick up a defender for a lead block, Young sprinted behind him on a bootleg. The quarterback then set his feet midway through his jaunt and fired a dart over the middle to tight end Tommy Tremble in the end zone. Before the ball even reached the wide-open Tremble's hands, Young turned around and threw up a touchdown signal as a way of celebrating the 12-yard heave for a go-ahead score. The oft soft-spoken signal-caller showed off his understated bravado with the early commemoration of the touchdown connection. "It was the coolest thing ever," Tremble said about Young's signature throw of 2024. "That play is one of my favorites. Like, it's fun to see, and that's when I feel like Bryce Young really, like, activated and everyone else could see the kind of player he was." The Panthers won the 2024 season finale against the Falcons on the road, 44-38, in overtime, as Young produced a career-high five total touchdowns -- three with his arm and two with his legs -- nearly four months after he was benched in Week 3 of his second campaign. The shot of Young's pre-completion celebration spread throughout the 2025 offseason and served as a beacon of hope for fans of the much-maligned passer. "He was the best dude on the field," Panthers right guard Rob Hunt said. "That was cool. ... It was a good moment for him, for sure -- confidence builder. ...That was good going into the next season." And while Young did improve throughout his 2025 season, it was again his bout against the Falcons on the road last season that turned heads. In his Atlanta-based follow-up to the 2024 clash, Young threw for a franchise-record 448 yards -- surpassing Cam Newton's previous mark of 432 yards in 2011 -- and three touchdowns in a 30-27 overtime win against the Falcons. While the Panthers head back to Atlanta on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) with an identical 0-1 record to the Falcons, Young's previous two trips to Mercedes-Benz Stadium should keep Falcons fans and coaches up at night. And considering the Panthers' defense gave up 59 points and 552 yards to the Chicago Bears last week, Young -- who led six scoring drives in Week 1 -- might need to be the difference-maker again on Sunday. "Coach [ Dave Canales ] talks about it all the time: Our first goal is to win the [NFC] South," Young said Wednesday. "And obviously, those division wins mean so much, when you're trying to accomplish that goal. You have the same process and you understand that. You don't want to get too high or too low, but again, this is a business, we're all pros and we understand what's at stake every time that it's a division opponent." Let's look closer at how Young has gone above and beyond inside the dome that sits in the heart of Atlanta and get a feel for what the 25-year-old could do for an encore. Young's performances in Atlanta Despite losing his NFL debut in Atlanta in the season opener against the Falcons in 2023, Young's numbers against his familiar foes run counter to his overall career stat line. Young had a 16.4 total quarterback rating in his debut loss against the Falcons, but he has since won four consecutive starts against Atlanta, raising his QBR against the rival NFC South franchise to 67.4, which is more than 20 points higher than his career number of 43.9. Young is 4-1 in his starts against the Falcons and 10-30 as a starter against everyone else. His 66.7% completion percentage against Atlanta is five percentage points higher than his career average (61.4%). In five games, Young has thrown for 1,133 passing yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. He is throwing 3.5 touchdowns for every interception against Atlanta; he averages 1.7 touchdowns per interception against the entire league. The QB has also scored a third of his career rushing touchdowns against the Falcons, as three of his nine QB-keeper TDs have come against Atlanta. "I feel like every single time he goes to Atlanta, he just makes the plays," Tremble said. "And him breaking Cam Newton's passing record that game [in 2025] -- it was sick to see. It was fun to be a part of that. So, I'm excited to see him, hopefully, even top that game from last time." And while his numbers are comparatively modest at home in Charlotte (288 total passing yards, 17 rushing total yards and a rushing touchdown in two games) against the Falcons, his last two road trips to Atlanta featured 699 total passing yards, 23 total rushing yards and eight total touchdowns to go with a pair of overtime victories in thrilling shootouts. It's also worth noting, Young's success at Mercedes-Benz Stadium predates his NFL career. He threw for 765 total yards and seven total touchdowns in two blowout wins in Atlanta during his tenure as the Alabama Crimson Tide's starting QB. During one of those outings, he also ran for 40 yards and a touchdown on three carries -- to go along with 421 passing yards and three passing touchdowns -- against Georgia in the 2021 SEC championship game. Young's outlook against Falcons in Week 2 Young's fourth Week 1 appearance went much better than his previous three opening-week outings for Carolina. He finished the 59-37 loss to the Bears with 361 passing yards, four total touchdowns (including a rushing score) and an interception. He had a 66.4 QBR, nearly identical to his overall success against Atlanta. "He's off to a hot start right now, we've just got to keep it rolling," Tremble said. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Young threw for a career-high 221 yards on deep throws against Chicago, completing 64.3% of his downfield heaves. He was particularly effective against zone coverage, throwing for 289 yards compared to 72 yards against man coverage. Against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, the Falcons ran zone coverage on nearly 40% of their defensive snaps. Atlanta favored man coverage at nearly 60% against Pittsburgh. Young will need to be much more efficient against man coverage than he was against the Bears, who primarily used zone coverage against Carolina in Week 1. Still, Young faced coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's scheme twice last season, and while the quarterback had a modest stat line in their initial meeting in Charlotte (121 passing yards, eight rushing yards and a rushing touchdown with 66.7% completion percentage), he exploded to boast career-high passing numbers in the second go-around in Atlanta in 2025. Nothing should be particularly foreign to Young about Ulbrich's attack, even with coach Kevin Stefanski now overseeing the team. "Very matchy group, guys that -- especially on the perimeter -- they play really well," Young said about the man coverage-heavy scheme. "Understand concepts, do a great job of pattern matching, all that stuff, so we know it's going to take everything. We have to be executing at a high level to have success." Biggest X factor for Young in Atlanta? The Panthers' offensive line needs to keep Young upright Sunday. Against Chicago, Young was pressured on 11 of his 41 dropbacks, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also took two sacks. Carolina will go up against new faces on the Falcons front, too. With defensive ends James Pearce Jr . (suspension) and Jalon Walker (injured reserve) unavailable, Atlanta will count on veterans Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam to bring the pressure, along with newly acquired defensive tackles Maason Smith and Gervon Dexter Sr . Against Pittsburgh, Za'Darius Smith picked up both of the Falcons' sacks and the front seven pressured Rodgers on 13 of his 40 dropbacks (31%), according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Young's escapability is crucial for big gains in both phases, but he also can't be scrambling in and out of the pocket on every play. Fill-in starting tackles Rasheed Walker and rookie Monroe Freeling did a solid enough job of protecting Young in their debut as a tandem and the interior line held its own as well. "They definitely have lost a lot of their edge defenders, just due to injuries and other circumstances, but the guys that I have seen so far, they're good at their bull rushes," Freeling said. "... So for me, it's just going to be important anchoring and making sure [the rushers] don't collapse the pocket, so Bryce has as much space as he needs to work." If the offensive line can hold up against Atlanta, Young could extend plays and toss the ball down the field with authority, perhaps with some more pre-completion showmanship. play 0:47 The good and the bad with the Panthers offense Projected stat line for Young's Week 2 ESPN senior writer Mike Clay has projected Young's stat line for Week 2 . While Clay doesn't have Young matching his heroics from the previous two trips down South, he does have the Panthers QB putting together a quality performance against the Falcons. Clay projects Young to complete 21 of 33 passes (63.3%) for 236 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while adding three carries for 19 rushing yards.

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Baltimore Ravens; Los Angeles Rams Anthony Gharib Sep 17, 2026, 03:23 PM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Uniforms revealed in the offseason will make their respective debuts in Week 2. Fresh from their trip Down Under, the Los Angeles Rams look to win their first game of the season with a design rooted in its history. Los Angeles will wear its "Classic Sol" alternate threads against the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football." The uniform honors the Rams' championship in 1951, with this season marking the 75th anniversary. A sol-colored jersey includes royal blue stitched and colored numbers. The three-stripe royal blue sleeve design is a direct nod to the uniforms worn in the 1951 season. The Giants will counter by going all-white. The Baltimore Ravens underwent a closet redesign in the offseason , and with it came a new helmet and combination. Nicknamed "White Noise," Baltimore will pair all-white threads with the "Purple Rising" helmet against the New Orleans Saints . Baltimore originally revealed the purple lids in 2024, but tweaked them in April with a logo change, maintaining the metallic purple. It tops off a sleek new all-white look. It's an all-white look for the New York Jets as well, but from head-to-toe. New York unveiled new white helmets in July that differ from the throwback ones it typically wears with its classic uniforms. The Jets will pair it together with all-white jerseys and pants against the Green Bay Packers , who will wear their traditional home green on the road. In the NFL "Rivalries" space, the Arizona Cardinals are the first to wear their design this season. Revealed last year, Arizona will rock it versus the Seattle Seahawks -- the same team they debuted it against in the previous campaign. Here's a look at the Week 2 uniforms for all 32 NFL teams. Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Stephen A.: Josh Allen, Bills made a statement with win over Texans (2:09) ESPN staff Sep 17, 2026, 09:00 AM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The Buffalo Bills play their first regular-season game at Highmark Stadium on Thursday, officially opening their new home field. Buffalo broke ground on the more than $2.1 billion stadium , which holds a capacity of 60,108, 10,000 fewer than its previous home, in May 2023. Highmark Stadium boasts specific features to combat the Buffalo weather. It includes a natural grass field with underground heating coils to prevent it from freezing. There's the world's largest stadium snow-melt system that automatically monitors and melts snow accumulations using roof sensors. A 360-degree canopy -- which covers 60% of the seating bowl -- reduces the impact of the wind. Safe to say, the Bills' new stomping grounds include elements unseen across the league. First on the docket for Buffalo at home? The Detroit Lions on "Thursday Night Football." As Buffalo opens its new stadium, here's a look back at notable opening games at NFL teams' active stadiums. Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas Raiders , 2020 Less than a year after their final game in Oakland, the Raiders officially completed their move to Las Vegas by playing at their new home, Allegiant Stadium. It's one of the most expensive sports venues in the world and has a capacity of 65,000, but it opened in the midst of the coronavirus. Therefore, no fans were allowed in the stadium for the opener. The Raiders still managed to put on a show on "Monday Night Football." Las Vegas fell into a 10-0 first quarter deficit to the New Orleans Saints , but outscored them 34-14 the rest of the way to win. Raiders quarterback Derek Carr had 284 passing yards and three touchdowns, while tight end Darren Waller caught 12 passes for 105 yards and a score. SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles Rams and Chargers , 2020 Built at a cost of over $5 billion , SoFi Stadium is the most expensive sports stadium in the world. It seats approximately 70,000 fans and could be expanded for as many 100,000 attendees. At 3.1 million square feet, it's the largest NFL stadium. Its two tenants, the Los Angeles Rams and Chargers, had separate debuts at SoFi with contrasting results. The Rams had first dibs, playing on "Sunday Night Football" against the Dallas Cowboys . They beat the Cowboys 20-17 in a back-and-forth game. The Chargers followed the Rams up with an overtime defeat to the Kansas City Chiefs a week later. That first SoFi game for the Chargers marked quarterback Justin Herbert's NFL debut. He threw for 311 yards and had a touchdown on the ground and in the air. Herbert joined Cam Newton and Otto Graham as the only quarterbacks to throw for 300 yards and have a rushing touchdown in their first game. Levi's Stadium, San Francisco 49ers , 2014 The 49ers spent over 40 years at Candlestick Park before moving to the billion-dollar Levi's Stadium with a capacity of 68,500. And if the first game at the new arena was any indication, 49ers fans would've happily crawled back to Candlestick. The Chicago Bears scored 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to come back and defeat San Francisco 28-20 . Quarterback Colin Kaepernick threw consecutive interceptions in the fourth quarter, leading to touchdowns for Chicago. The 49ers had one last chance to tie it with 6:55 left in the game, but suffered a turnover on downs as the Bears spoiled the opening. MetLife Stadium, New York Giants and Jets , 2010 The old tenants of Giants Stadium moved to MetLife Stadium together, too. In front of just under 80,000 fans, the Giants had the opening game as they faced the Carolina Panthers , whom the Giants lost to in the final game of their old home. It was a different outcome than the previous meeting with the Giants defeating the Panthers 31-18 behind three touchdowns from quarterback Eli Manning. The next day, the Jets faced the Baltimore Ravens on "Monday Night Football." Fresh off a trip to the conference championship game, the Jets started off on the wrong foot, losing to Baltimore in a low-scoring 10-9 affair. Cowboys Stadium, Dallas Cowboys, 2009 Dubbed "Jerry's World," the opening of AT&T Stadium was a true spectacle with over 100,000 attendees. Celebrities flocked to the game, including former President George W. Bush, who did the coin toss, and LeBron James, who threw a football on the field. There was the debut of the massive jumbotron and fireworks to ring in the arena on "Sunday Night Football." The Giants weren't phased by any of it. The two teams traded jabs all night before New York laid the final punch. After the Cowboys went up 31-30 with over three minutes left in the game, the Giants drove down for a game-winning 37-yard field goal as time expired, stunning the crowd. Giants quarterback Eli Manning signed the visiting locker room wall after the game, writing the date, final score and "first win in the new stadium." Reliant Stadium, Houston Texans , 2002 The NFL's most recent expansion team, the Houston Texans, opened their stadium in front of just under 70,000 fans on "Sunday Night Football" against the Cowboys. Houston had the previous draft's No. 1 pick David Carr under center, and he delivered immediately. The Texans scored 75 seconds in, sending the crowd into a frenzy. Houston never trailed again en route to a 19-10 victory. It became the first expansion team to win its debut since 1961.

Mike is a member of the FSWA Hall of Fame. His projections power the ESPN Fantasy Football game, and he also appears on "Fantasy Football Now" and the Fantasy Focus Football podcast. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Welcome to The Playbook for Week 2, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Lions and Bills . This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices. Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week. If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet . You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule as it stood before the season. All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense. DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)
