He joined ESPN in 2017 after covering the team for Seattle Sports 710-AM. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The Seattle Seahawks have ruled out Sam Darnold for their game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, but coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday that there are no plans to place the quarterback on injured reserve. Darnold is dealing with a glute injury that knocked him out of Seattle's season opener. An IR stint would require him to miss at least the next four games, so keeping Darnold on the 53-man roster indicates the Seahawks believe he has a chance to return before then. Drew Lock will start for Seattle in Darnold's absence. Following the Arizona game, the reigning Super Bowl champions will visit the Washington Commanders in Week 3, then host the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4 and the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, multiple sources are bracing for Darnold to miss roughly four weeks from the time of his injury but are hoping he can come back sooner. One source told Fowler that Darnold returning for the 49ers game in Week 5 feels like a possibility. Another source estimated that he'll be sidelined for three to four weeks and added that the quarterback is moving around much better in recent days. In a statement to local reporters on Monday, the Seahawks described Darnold as having a "very unique soft-tissue" injury. "Don't anticipate putting him on IR or anything like that, but we'll just kind of re-evaluate every day and re-evaluate next week and we'll go from there," Macdonald said Wednesday. "But he won't play this week." Darnold's injury is in the area of his right glute. He was hurt on the fifth play of the opener when his right knee hit the turf as he was being sacked from behind. He hobbled off the field, then limped into the locker room after being examined in the medical tent. The Seahawks eventually ruled Darnold out with what they announced as a hip injury. He was taken to Harborview Medical Center for testing during the game and stayed there overnight, in part because of how much discomfort he was in. Darnold was not on the field Monday or Wednesday during the warmup period of Seahawks practice, which is all media members are allowed to view. "He's killing it on his rehab," Macdonald said. "He's going a great job. He's doing a lot right now. He's just not going to be able to play this week." Lock, who stepped in for Darnold and quarterbacked the Seahawks to a 13-10 win over the New England Patriots last Wednesday, is in line to make his first start since 2024. The 29-year-old quarterback has a 10-18 career record as a starter since entering the league as a second-round pick by the Denver Broncos in 2019. He went 8-13 over three seasons with the Broncos before they dealt him to Seattle in the 2022 Russell Wilson trade. Lock went 1-1 for the Seahawks in 2023, then 1-4 for the New York Giants in 2024 before returning to Seattle last year to back up Darnold. Against New England, Lock completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards, a touchdown and zero turnovers. "Drew's a proven, really good player in this league," Macdonald said. "When he's started, he's played really good football. When he's been on our team since I've seen him play in person, he's [been] a heck of a player here. Heck of a guy. Heck of a teammate. He's got a great balance about him of being a true professional, but also, he's a loose and focused guy ... All the things that we want from our players, he's that at the quarterback position." Jalen Milroe , a 2025 second-round pick, is Seattle's third quarterback. The team has yet to bring in another quarterback for a tryout. When asked if the Seahawks plan to add a another QB, Macdonald said they're "going to roll with Drew and Jalen." In other Seahawks injury news, Macdonald said safety Nick Emmanwori (ankle) and wide receiver Tory Horton (hamstring) are practicing Wednesday. Both missed the opener. "Those guys are doing great," Macdonald said "They're going to practice today and we'll go from there." Macdonald said safety Ty Okada (hamstring) has a chance to play Sunday after missing Week 1.

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions CINCINNATI -- A back injury isn't going to keep Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow from playing this weekend against the Houston Texans . Burrow is dealing with back tightness following the team's Week 1 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . He made no significant throws during the open portion of practice and, when asked about his workload Wednesday, said he got in "mental reps." But the idea of not facing the Texans for precautionary reasons? "That's ridiculous," Burrow said. Burrow isn't sure when he sustained the injury but said he started to feel soreness in the hours following Sunday's game. He was sacked only once. However, he took a hard hit when scrambling for a first down. The play extended the drive, which ended with a touchdown pass. Even in hindsight, Burrow was OK with the result. "I was comfortable with it," Burrow said. "It was either that or kick a field goal. It's a decision that I made." The two-time MVP finalist has dealt with injuries during much of his seven-year career. Last season, a turf toe injury forced him to miss nine games in the middle of the season. It was the third time he had been placed on injured reserve. Throughout the offseason, Burrow talked about an increased level of urgency heading into this season. After making deep playoff runs in 2021 and 2022, including a Super Bowl appearance at the start of that run, Cincinnati has missed the playoffs in each of the last three years. His heightened expectations for this season will not play a role in his decision to play in Houston. "I think every game is important," Burrow said. "I'll do what it takes to be out there. If I'm not having surgery, I'll be out there." Burrow is used to playing through injuries. In 2022, Burrow didn't miss any games despite undergoing an emergency appendectomy at the beginning of training camp that left him briefly hospitalized. The following year, Burrow also didn't skip any snaps despite suffering a strained calf in preseason that he aggravated in Week 2. Speaking to reporters Wednesday, the three-time Pro Bowler said he is still trying to find the balance of when to take risks when on the field. In the season-opening win against the Buccaneers, Burrow was 25-of-35 passing for 254 yards, one touchdown and one interception that was returned for a score. "You have to think about the situation of the game, what kind of game are you in," Burrow said. "That's something I'm still working on, for sure." Last season marked the first time in Burrow's career that the Bengals started a season with two straight wins. But it came at a cost. On a play that was designed to be a quick pass, Burrow was sacked as he extended the play and his foot was caught in the turf at Paycor Stadium. This weekend, Burrow and the Bengals will have a tough task against a Houston defense that features two premier edge rushers in Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr . "We certainly have our work cut out for us," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Wednesday. "They have elite talent across the board on their defense, and it poses a lot of challenges for you." If Cincinnati wins and Burrow doesn't sustain any significant damage, the Bengals will be off to the best start since Burrow was drafted with the No. 1 pick in 2020. But that was far from Burrow's mind Wednesday afternoon. "We're taking it one week at a time," he said. "We're excited about the opportunity this week."

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens placed wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane on injured reserve after the promising rookie had surgery on his fractured wrist Wednesday morning. Lane, who had been one of the Ravens' stars in training camp and preseason, is expected to return as soon as he's eligible to come off IR in four weeks. "[Lane] definitely has a really good chance coming back here pretty quick," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "I know he'll be chomping at the bit to get back." A third-round pick in this year's draft, Lane quickly rose up the depth chart this summer with highlight catches nearly every day in camp and entered the season as Baltimore's No. 3 receiver behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman . In the 41-23 season-opening win at the Colts, Lane finished with one catch for 11 yards, but he had a 4-yard touchdown catch nullified because of a holding penalty. Lane injured a wrist in the first half and didn't return after halftime. "He's definitely beating himself up about it, but it's only so much he can control," Bateman said. "Injuries are part of the game, and his is unfortunate. But whenever he comes back, he'll be ready." Flowers didn't practice Wednesday after aggravating his left hamstring Sunday. He led Baltimore with 150 yards receiving before hurting his hamstring with about 5½ minutes left in the first half. Flowers, who is Lamar Jackson 's top target, remains day-to-day. "I think he's in a really good place," Minter said. If Flowers can't play Sunday against the New Orleans Saints , Bateman becomes the most experienced wide receiver and will likely receive increased opportunities. The Ravens' other wide receivers on the 53-man roster -- Devontez Walker , LaJohntay Wester , Elijah Sarratt and Chris Moore -- have a combined 21 catches over the last three seasons. Minter's message to the healthy wide receivers: "Run at the opportunity." "We got a lot of confidence in all those guys," Minter said. "They've gotten so many reps from all the way back from the offseason program to now ... just go out there and use the talent that you've been given."

Cockcroft is senior writer for fantasy baseball and football at ESPN. Tristan is a member of the FSWA Hall of Fame. He is also two-time LABR and four-time Tout Wars champion. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of the fantasy football process. When you're torn between two similar players and simply don't know which to start, start the player with the superior matchup. Ah, but exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups? The matchup rankings provide a schedule-independent method to evaluate positional matchups each week, ranking all 32 opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at all four skill positions (quarterback, running back, wide receiver and tight end). Instead of relying upon seasonal totals, we calibrate points-allowed data to show how each defense fared relative to the difficulty of the schedule it has faced. This provides a fairer approach to judging the quality of individual matchups. For the first three weeks, these rankings account for two things: my own opinion of the strength of that matchup, and what ESPN's projections tell us about it. As an additional reference point, 2025 full-season data is provided. "Adj. FPA," or adjusted fantasy points allowed, reflects how far above or below players' weekly PPR fantasy point averages that defense held opponents at that position. A positive number means the matchup is favorable; a negative number means it is unfavorable. Also, remember teams often use multiple running backs and wide receivers in a game, and these plus/minus averages cover all of a team's personnel at that position. Finally, a caveat: Matchups are only one ingredient in my rankings formula. Not every favorable matchup should be exploited, nor every unfavorable matchup avoided. If you want my -- and the ESPN fantasy staff's -- most complete source for whom to start and sit each week, consult our weekly rankings . Quarterbacks Matchups highlight: Dak Prescott , Dallas Cowboys (vs. Washington Commanders ). His Week 1 (14.40 fantasy points) wasn't anything special, but in his defense, his Cowboys committed multiple drops and five offensive penalties, and it's worth noting that opening-week struggles are part of his personal history (he hasn't scored as many as 15 points in a Week 1 since 2021). A Week 2 matchup against the Commanders, at home no less, is a much softer matchups landing spot. The Commanders surrendered 20.12 fantasy points on only 25 passing plays to Jalen Hurts in Week 1, and Prescott himself has scored in excess of 20 fantasy points in four straight home games overall and in each of his past five home games against the Commanders. Others to like: Brock Purdy , San Francisco 49ers (vs. Miami Dolphins ); C.J. Stroud , Houston Texans (vs. Cincinnati Bengals ). Matchup to avoid: Joe Burrow , Bengals (at Texans). After Josh Allen dropped 35.66 fantasy points on the vaunted Texans defense -- a total more than 15 better than any other quarterback scored against it in 2025 -- Burrow's managers might be brimming with confidence over his prospects facing the same matchup. Pump the brakes, as 40% of Allen's production came on rushing plays, an area that has not been Burrow's forte, while much of the Texans' defensive issues could be pinned squarely on their difficulty handling Allen's mobility. This is still an upper-quarter defense, and Burrow averaged 3.4 fewer fantasy points against upper-quarter defenses than the rest of the league the past two seasons. Running backs Matchups highlight: David Montgomery , Texans (vs. Bengals). A human touchdown machine in Week 1, Montgomery had five goal-to-go touches (four carries, one target) and converted three for scores in the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills. His status as the team's clear goal-line back will prove important against the Bengals, who surrendered 19 yards and two touchdowns to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on three goal-to-go plays last week. Bucky Irving , one of the league's least effective goal-line backs in his two-plus years in the league (22.2% touchdown rate on goal-to-go plays), managed 20.3 fantasy points in that game. Others to like: Jadarian Price , Seattle Seahawks (at Arizona Cardinals ); Jacory Croskey-Merritt , Commanders (at Cowboys). Matchup to avoid: Cam Skattebo , New York Giants (at Los Angeles Rams ). His return game from a dislocated ankle couldn't have gone much better -- 14.1 fantasy points and 25 rushing yards over expected, per Next Gen Stats -- but the Rams represent significant contrast to a Cowboys matchup. The Rams, despite a disappointing teamwide performance in Australia last Thursday, held last season's top-scoring running back, Christian McCaffrey , to 13.8 fantasy points on 15 touches. They were also the seventh-best schedule-adjusted defense against the position in 2025. Skattebo's big-play ability gives him a solid ceiling even facing this matchup, but he's also a highly risky play. Wide receivers Matchups highlight: Terry McLaurin , Commanders (at Cowboys). From a matchup to avoid to the week's highlight, such is the contrast between McLaurin's first two games this season. As with the Philadelphia Eagles , last week's opponent, McLaurin has quite the history with the division-rival Cowboys, though this matchup has become more advantageous for the veteran wideout this season after the Cowboys released Trevon Diggs in December. The Cowboys' current defensive back combination of DaRon Bland , Cobie Durant and Jalen Thompson afforded Giants wide receivers a combined 22.1 fantasy points on 15 targets, and another 27.8 to tight end Isaiah Likely on eight targets, in Week 1. McLaurin has also gotten the better of the Cowboys the past two seasons, averaging 17.6 points in four meetings. Others to like: Mike Evans , 49ers (vs. Dolphins); DeVonta Smith , Eagles (at Tennessee Titans ); George Pickens , Cowboys (vs. Commanders). Matchup to avoid: Parker Washington , Jacksonville Jaguars (at Denver Broncos ). His 2026 debut was impressive, a 19.3 fantasy point effort highlighted by his 30-yard, diving touchdown reception on the opening drive. Unfortunately, he's in for a much taller task in Week 2, against a Broncos defense that, despite a mediocre overall performance on "Monday Night Football," limited Kansas City Chiefs wide receivers to a combined 14.7 fantasy points on 10 targets. Between the Jaguars' likelihood of spreading passes around all season and the presence of three-time All-Pro and 2024 Defensive Player of the Year CB Pat Surtain II on the Broncos' side, Washington should find it difficult to approach his opening-week number. Quarterback Rankings changes: We typically preach patience in this column, especially after one week of football , but it is hard to deny moving Chicago Bears starter Caleb Williams up. Not only might he be the first Bears QB to ever reach 4,000 passing yards or 30 touchdown passes, but he might do that before Thanksgiving. We did not significantly move the Cincinnati Bengals ' Joe Burrow , Kansas City Chiefs ' Patrick Mahomes or Denver Broncos ' Bo Nix , but we might soon. If you roster Kyler Murray (concussion) and Sam Darnold (glute) in deeper formats/superflex, try to keep them around. They fall some in the rankings, but they may return to active duty soon and provide value. Backups Carson Wentz and Drew Lock just barely enter the rankings, but if choosing between them, choose Wentz. Follow on X Multiple Authors Sep 16, 2026, 10:30 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions The 2026 NFL season is officially rolling. As we head into Week 2, insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz. Week 1 saw the Seahawks, Vikings and Falcons all forced to turn to backup quarterbacks -- and in Atlanta's case, it was a third-stringer. Where do those franchises sit at QB entering Week 2? Jeremy and Dan also asked around about a tough opening week for the two Los Angeles teams. Is there concern yet for the Rams and Chargers? Plus, they debated debuts for coaches and rookies then offered up their best fantasy tips based on what they're hearing. It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 2. Jump to: QB situations | Rams, Chargers concerns Coaching debuts | Rookie debuts Fantasy football takes | Notes and more buzz What's the latest on the quarterback situation for the Vikings, Seahawks and Falcons? Graziano: Things seem straightforward for Minnesota. Based on what I've been able to gather, my sense is that Kyler Murray will start if he clears concussion protocol in time, and Carson Wentz is likely to start if Murray isn't clear in time. That sounds like a negative toward J.J. McCarthy , since it was him and not Wentz who competed with Murray for the starting job in camp. But this is more about the Vikings believing Wentz's veteran experience puts them in better position with limited preparation time when a QB gets hurt in-game (as happened Sunday) and/or there's uncertainty about who's going to start throughout the week. McCarthy was the emergency third QB on Sunday, so the team knew there was a chance they might have to play him. I could see a scenario in which Wentz starts this week with McCarthy as the backup, assuming Murray can't go. Fowler: That's certainly plausible. Murray took a nasty hit, and teams tend to be overly cautious when a player has assumed the fencing position, for good reason. But how players work through the five stages of the protocol often varies, so it's tough to know Murray's timeline at this point. Wentz is set up for success in Week 2 . He got hot last week versus Green Bay , and Chicago just allowed 361 passing yards to Bryce Young . In Seattle, it's clear Sam Darnold will miss this week and possibly Week 3. But the Seahawks have refrained from putting him on short-term injured reserve, which is a good sign. The team seems confident that Drew Lock is plug and play until Darnold returns. Graziano: Yeah, Seattle believes Lock can handle it, so he's the guy there for the foreseeable future. I'm personally interested to see whether they put in anything specific for Jalen Milroe in terms of plays or packages that take advantage of his running ability and maybe give their offense a little bit extra juice. Why not, if Milroe is going to be active anyway as the second quarterback? What about Atlanta? Kevin Stefanski probably thought he left the QB mess behind in Cleveland, but he has a situation on his hands, no? Fowler: Stefanski has seen it all at quarterback, but at least his signal-callers in Cleveland mostly stayed out of the training room. Tua Tagovailoa 's body seems to be betraying him at an inopportune time. The Falcons' best option remains third-year man Michael Penix Jr. , but he's not yet ready for live game action. Penix wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field following left ACL surgery in November. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him. Tagovailoa's injury, an oblique strain , can linger, which puts his Week 2 status up in the air. So, Cooper Rush starting another week wouldn't be shocking. What helps Tagovailoa's case is his accuracy, which Stefanski highly values. If Tagovailoa's body doesn't totally break down in the short term and he can return before Penix is ready, perhaps Tagovailoa can provide a spark. Graziano: Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction , which is a lot of ACL reconstructions. I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it's OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I'm sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season. The Falcons are going to want to know whether he is a real long-term option moving forward. My sense is Tagovailoa was the favorite to start at the beginning of camp even when Penix was healthy but that Tagovailoa didn't perform the way the team had hoped he would. That has turned things into a confusing mess. Fowler: That two-week stretch, from the second preseason game rolling into the joint practice with the Colts, was rough for Tagovailoa. The schedule provides another wrinkle. Atlanta will play on Thursday night in Week 3, so even if Penix is close, that might not be the best week to reacclimate him. How high is the panic level in the Rams' building? What about for the Chargers? Fowler: Well, the Rams' top-ranked offense scored seven points , and the league's best pass rusher is out at least a month . But other than that, everything's fine! I don't, however, sense heavy panic from the Rams, who seemed to approach the Australia trip with the excitement of a teenager asked to take out the trash. 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris knows the Rams' offense well, so San Francisco's ability to stymie Matthew Stafford shouldn't be a total shock. The Myles Garrett situation is more alarming. The Rams thought they could manage his knee injury with rest all camp and preseason, and it got exposed in Week 1. It leaves some uneasiness that they perhaps should have had this injury surgically repaired a tad sooner. But the Rams have plenty of defensive talent to offset the Garrett loss. Graziano: Garrett missed basically an entire month's worth of training camp with the knee problem, so those of us on the outside should have considered that a possible warning sign, at the very least. Aaron Donald being able to play Monday night would help, but the issues that came up in Australia went beyond Garrett's health. The Rams' expensive new cornerback tandem looked miscast in the defensive game plan, and they couldn't get the passing game clicking. The Rams are certainly not going to panic because of one game, even if it was an embarrassing loss to a division rival. But they are (and should be) taking the problems that were on display against the 49ers seriously. The operation needs to be sharper on both sides of the ball. One possible benefit of the Rams' controversial Australian travel plan is that they likely didn't need to get reacclimated upon their return home, since their body clocks theoretically never reset in the first place. We'll see if they come out looking sharper in Week 2 against the Giants. play 2:16 Why Stephen A. says the Rams should exhibit patience with Aaron Donald Fowler: The Chargers' panic meter will rise if they lose to the Raiders this week . Arizona was deemed terrible in the preseason, but the Cardinals are more respectable than that, particularly on offense. So, the Chargers' defense gets a mulligan after seeing the Cards in the opener. It's a veteran group that should improve. The bigger concern is how the Bolts' offense looked after wide receiver Ladd McConkey left the game with a rib injury. McConkey and Justin Herbert showed easy chemistry in that first half. They need McConkey, who is listed as day-to-day , to work his way back or concerns about the offensive attack will mushroom. I'm expecting a better running game from Los Angeles in Week 2 as it tries to find some continuity with the offensive line. Graziano: McConkey is a great player, but the game plan falling apart completely once he exited makes it seem as if it was flimsy to begin with. Where are the smart, creative run plays Mike McDaniel was calling last season in Miami? Wasn't running back Omarion Hampton supposed to explode in this scheme? Wasn't the wide receiver group supposed to be deep with talent? Were the Chargers gaslighting us all summer? This was so far off our expectations for the Herbert-McDaniel pairing that you have to wonder whether L.A. took the Cardinals seriously enough. But you're absolutely right, Jeremy. The Chargers need to beat the Raiders this week and look good doing it or we're going to wonder if it was all hype. Being 0-2 and looking up at the 2-0 Raiders in the AFC West standings would not feel good for a team that had the preseason hopes the Chargers held. But Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby isn't going to make life any easier on that offensive line, which struggled with protection in the first game. Which new coach's debut surprised you the most in Week 1? Graziano: The Cardinals' Mike LaFleur. I figured they'd have a representative offense, because I believe LaFleur is a talented offensive mind who knows how to call a game and put his players in the best position to take advantage of their strengths. But Arizona was good all over the field and dictated the action for much of Sunday's game. That says a lot about what LaFleur has been able to establish in terms of confidence and buy-in in a short period of time. Very impressive. Fowler: It's early, but LaFleur seems to have a good sense of what it takes to be successful, with a blend of hard-nosed coaching and relatability that comes out in his news conferences and on the sidelines. I'd caution that Arizona started 2-0 last season before cratering, but its operation looks improved overall. I was surprised Cleveland didn't play better under Todd Monken. Maybe I shouldn't have been since the offense is so young (six first- or second-year starters). But the 60-year-old Monken has waited decades for this opportunity, and his entire team was flat in Jacksonville . The outcry from fans will only intensify if quarterback Deshaun Watson plays poorly again. Graziano: It's hard for me to be surprised when someone who insists on starting Watson at quarterback in 2026 doesn't have success. There are some things to like about Cleveland's roster, and I believe Monken knows how to coach, but the Browns aren't going anywhere with Watson. Until they admit that and make a change, I don't see how things can improve. Just horrendous vibes all the way around. I have to say that Buffalo's Joe Brady probably had the best Week 1 win of the new coaches, prevailing on the road against Houston. Having spent a little time around the Bills before and after Sunday's game, it feels as if Brady is connecting with that group on a level that goes beyond his abilities as an offensive playcaller. Fowler: Also, Jesse Minter winning his first game as the Ravens' coach wasn't a surprise, but the fashion in which his squad bounced Indianapolis was. Baltimore's offense was in complete control, and the defense forced two turnovers. Minter is known as a teacher/tactician, and the Ravens embodied that approach with minimal mistakes in Week 1. Which rookie debut is drawing the most hype around the league? Fowler: The first-year edge rushers flashed. David Bailey came out hot for the Jets, which was no surprise in league circles. "He was the most polished pass rusher [in the draft], so he had the best chances to contribute early among the top rushers," an NFL personnel director said. And it was quite the contribution, as Bailey registered four tackles, six quarterback pressures and one sack in 34 defensive snaps against Tennessee . Speaking of rookie rushers, the Chiefs' R Mason Thomas recorded his first sack on a spin move Monday night versus Denver . Thomas' buzz in Kansas City is growing due to his high motor and pass-rush arsenal. Graziano: Buccaneers linebacker Josiah Trotter was tough to miss in his debut, with a sack and an interception return for a touchdown. Tampa Bay's second-round pick outshined Bucs first-rounder Rueben Bain Jr. , who had a tough time against massive Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims . I've also heard positive reviews on the debut of Giants guard Francis Mauigoa , who was part of a bruising rushing attack against the Cowboys on Sunday night. Fowler: Good call on Trotter. On the offensive side of the ball, Seahawks first-round running back Jadarian Price drew attention by the way he runs, not necessarily his modest Week 1 output (10 rushes, 52 yards). "He's a load," an AFC scout said. "I expect his profile to grow." Seattle has been very pleased with Price's acumen and has no problem getting him involved, though it is dedicated to a multiple-back approach. Ravens first-round guard Olaivavega Ioane looked imposing in Indianapolis . And third-round Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas ' five-catch, 94-yard debut confirmed what I was hearing: that Douglas had impressed everyone in Miami's building. Graziano: For sure on Douglas! Love it when camp buzz comes to life in Week 1. Commanders' third-round wideout Antonio Williams was less buzzy, but it seems as if he has a real role as a slot receiver, and he caught a touchdown pass in his debut. I foresee Williams' role growing in that offense as the season goes along. What is your best piece of fantasy football advice for this week? Graziano: I'd be trying to trade Houston running back David Montgomery . Yes, he had three touchdowns in his Texans debut . If you really believe he will score three touchdowns every week, you should not trade him for anything. I personally do not think he's going to do that. I'm looking at Montgomery's 3.0 yards per carry against a Bills defense that was miserable against the run last season and the fact that Woody Marks was on the field for 40 snaps as compared with Montgomery's 39. The Texans were very impressed with the way Marks performed during the offseason, and they plan a significant role for the ball carrier in the offense. Montgomery got the Week 1 glory, but this might be a chance to sell high and claim a Week 1 underperformer who has a chance to pop in the coming weeks. play 0:56 Why David Montgomery's fantasy Week 1 went 'as well as you could've hoped' Fowler: Stick with Carolina wide receiver Jalen Coker (though maybe not this week). It would be silly to expect Coker to regularly break off 33-plus points like he did in Week 1 , but he's clearly part of the Panthers' offensive fabric alongside wideout Tetairoa McMillan . Coker is a primary deep threat, and quarterback Bryce Young trusts him. Coker was a good value play before the Week 1 breakout. He is nursing an ankle sprain , which is something to consider for Week 2, but the Panthers' offense appears set for a jump, and Coker will be part of that. Carolina's coaches are very high on him. What else are you hearing this week? Fowler: Here in Buffalo, where I'm prepping for the Thursday night game against Detroit , the synergy between Josh Allen and new coach Joe Brady is hard to miss. Brady has played a big hand in streamlining things for Allen, who has reduced turnovers and -- based on Sunday's win over Houston -- looks like he knows exactly where he wants to go with the ball at all times. Brady said Allen wants to be challenged -- and coached. When I asked Allen about that, he said the two have set goals for this season (which Allen won't be sharing). It's early, but the signs are that Allen is only getting better, and Brady said the two can experiment, succeed and fail together play-to-play. Allen is so locked in that he didn't bite when asked about the excitement around officially opening the $2.2 billion Highmark Stadium in earnest Thursday night. His message was clear: We have a job to do, and that's win, knowing the path to winning can change from week to week. This week, it could lead to a recharged running game. James Cook III is coming off a modest 13-carry, 57-yard performance. Brady says he has no reservations feeding him. "He's one of the best backs in football," Brady said. A few other Buffalo notes: Dalton Kincaid is high on Detroit's scouting report after his 130-yard performance. He's looking more slippery now that he's healthy. ... Greg Rousseau might prove to be the defensive closer Buffalo needs. He's in Year 6 and only 26 years old, so he's still coming into his own. Rousseau told me Jim Leonhard's defense provides extra one-on-one opportunities for him, on which he plans to capitalize (and did with two sacks in Week 1). ... The Bills practiced on newly laid Highmark Stadium sod Tuesday. The players were happier with the results compared to the preseason. Graziano: DJ Moore 's Bills debut was exciting, but Kincaid had more receiving yards (130 to 100) and could be the real key to elevating Josh Allen and the Buffalo offense this season. I was at the Bills' game in Houston, and multiple people with the team told me Kincaid is healthier than he was this time last year and is on no snap restrictions. The Bills want to be able to put multiple tight ends on the field at the same time, and the trio of Kincaid, Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes could be a formidable one. They're happy with the improvements Kincaid has shown as a blocker, but he's going to make his biggest contributions as a receiver and should have a greater impact when they have multiple tight ends in the formation. The Bills also believe their passing game can show even more than it did Sunday once pass-catching running back Ty Johnson is back healthy. Johnson was able to practice late last week and early this week, and he should be back soon. play 2:09 Stephen A.: Josh Allen, Bills made a statement with win over Texans The Bills' defense under Leonhard remains a bit of a work-in-progress entering the season, but you saw how disruptive Rousseau and Deone Walker were able to be up front, especially in the later stages of the game in Houston, and you can start to see which players are likely to thrive in the new system. Landon Jackson (2025 third-round pick) and Javon Solomon (2024 fifth-round pick) are two others to watch, as I'm told the system fits them well. And of course Ed Oliver remains their most important player up front and has taken to it as well. GM Brandon Beane said Leonard "is not one of those guys who's going to go square peg, round hole. He's all about 'give me good football players, we'll get them in the right spot.'" Much of this season on defense will be about the Bills seeing who develops and thrives in Leonard's system and figuring out what kinds of tweaks need to be made before next season. In the meantime, though, they believe they have the pieces to make it work in Year 1. Graziano: As for Houston, the Texans want to keep running the ball a bit on offense. (Hence why I think Montgomery and Marks are both worth having in fantasy, as mentioned above.) First-round rookie Keylan Rutledge has brought old-school toughness to the guard position, and tight end Dalton Schultz told me the offense's "mindset" is different this season. The unit has been able to dictate some of the action against the defense in practice -- "just growing into that confidence that comes from going against one of the best defenses in the league every day, taking on that challenge and showing improvement consistently." Schultz and other Texans told me they've noticed a sharper "edge" to quarterback C.J. Stroud this season, too. The way Sunday's game ended on a sack-fumble was unfortunate for Stroud, but his performance prior to that reflected some of what the Texans think they can be on offense. Watch for a larger role for newly acquired wide receiver Kayshon Boutte in the coming weeks. Graziano: Boutte's old team, the Patriots, might be regretting trading him away in the wake of the A.J. Brown injury . Brown is out at least four weeks, and the Patriots don't really have a one-for-one replacement on their roster. Second-year speedster Kyle Williams is likely to see more playing time, and Mack Hollins can do some of the stuff Brown can do as a physical, contested-catch guy down the field. But if the Patriots were satisfied with those players, they wouldn't have gone out and acquired Brown and Romeo Doubs in the offseason. The player they might be counting on that they didn't have last week is second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson , who can help in the passing game with his explosiveness out of the backfield. It's unclear at this time whether Henderson can make it back from his ankle injury in time for Sunday's game against the Steelers . Fowler: A new development in the Josh Jacobs criminal case emerged Tuesday, with the attorneys of his ex-girlfriend motioning for evidence in the criminal case to be permanently sealed. Attorneys Ramses Jalalpour and Amir Tahmassebi said in a statement, obtained by ESPN, that the motion is "consistent with our client's desire to protect her privacy, particularly in light of Mr. Jacobs taking responsibility for his actions in the criminal proceeding." The eight-page motion also states that the disclosure of evidence "would threaten ANM's (the woman) privacy, dignity, security and emotional well-being." A key issue here is the videotape of the incident with the ex-girlfriend -- and whether the NFL can get ahold of it. This motion makes it increasingly harder for the league to do so. My understanding is that, barring a formal appeal from one of the legal parties involved, that tape should remain tucked away. Last week, the court ordered Jacobs to pay restitution to the victim as part of his no contest plea for misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. It's quite possible, if not likely, that has already happened. He was also ordered to attend counseling and avoid contacting the victim. So, the NFL's investigation is ongoing, but there could be a suspension sooner rather than later. Jacobs remains on the commissioner exempt list. A four-to-six-game suspension could be the range based on a few people I've talked to in the league, but that's obviously fluid and based on the league's findings. Fowler: Jaguars receiver Parker Washington going for 83 yards and a touchdown Sunday was noteworthy since the player and team failed to reach a contract extension before Week 1. Washington can follow the Alec Pierce plan to free agency: ball out in Year 4 and push well past $25 million per year on a new deal. Pierce got four years, $114 million from Indy after recording his first 1,000-yard season. Fowler: Chiefs coach Andy Reid trusted undrafted Kahlil Benson at left tackle on Monday night against Denver and it paid off. Benson allowed one pressure in 32 pass-blocking snaps in the win. The Chiefs were evaluating Benson as a guard with tackle flexibility. But in the third preseason week, with Josh Simmons out , they slid Benson to left tackle for extended reps. He has acquitted himself well. The Simmons injury remains a mystery. In late August, he underwent tests on his back. Part of the testing was to see whether a disc issue had flared up. Information has been scarce since then. The Chiefs have treated this as if he's week-to-week. Meanwhile, they continue to rely on young players at several positions. Benson is the latest to shine. Also on the Chiefs front, free agent receiver Tyreek Hill remains fond of the Chiefs, and a potential in-season signing would make a lot of sense. He should be closer to playing around October. play 1:49 Why Stephen A. isn't declaring the Chiefs as team to beat in AFC Graziano: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers ' knee injury is not overly serious, from what I am told. The team felt he could have played last week if necessary, and it's possible he returns this week. But the organization is determined to be careful with this very important player and not play him until they're 100% certain he's not being affected by the knee. I believe the latest you'll see Bowers is Week 4 against the Chiefs, but again, it could be sooner than that. Fowler: The Ravens must adjust offensively due to receiver injuries. Rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is out for a while, and Zay Flowers reaggravated his hamstring issue , though that one is not considered serious. Expect Devontez Walker -- who was out last week -- to be up this week. He is also two-time LABR and four-time Tout Wars champion. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Updated Sept. 15, 2026 (through Week 1 of 2026) How consistency ratings work Using fantasy points determined by ESPN's standard scoring , the charts contained in this column rate players based upon how consistently reliable they have been during the 2024 through 2026 seasons, a span of 37 weeks' worth of games (18 weeks apiece in 2024 and 2025, one so far in 2026). For IDPs (individual defensive players), the scoring from our weekly rankings is used: solo tackle (1.5), assisted tackle (0.75), tackle for loss (2), sack (4), interception (5), forced fumble (4), fumble recovery (4), touchdown (6), safety (2), pass defended (1.5). To familiarize you with the terminology and column headers listed in the charts below: Start%: The player's "start percentage," which shows how often he earned a start in an ESPN standard PPR (points per reception) league. This is his number of "starts" -- those defined below -- divided by his number of scheduled team games. CR: The player's "consistency rating," which is calculated as his weekly standard deviation divided by his PPR fantasy points per game average. This is meant to identify the players who were most consistently close to their weekly averages. The lower the number, the more consistent the player. Again, lower numbers are better . nPPR%: The player's start percentage using non-PPR scoring, using ESPN's standard scoring settings without any points per reception. FPTS/G: The player's average PPR fantasy points scored per game. Start: The number of times that the player's point total in a given week was worthy of having had him active in an ESPN standard PPR league. Star: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the best at his position. Stiff: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the worst at his position, making almost any waiver-wire option a smarter choice. These are the benchmarks for what constitutes a "start," "star" or "stiff" performance: Sat: The number of times the player sat out a game. Players are not charged "stiff" points for sitting out, nor does it impact their overall consistency rating (CR), but it hurts their overall start percentage. Players must have a start rate of at least 20% in either standard PPR or non-PPR scoring, rank among the top 20 quarterbacks, tight ends or kickers, top 50 running backs or wide receivers, or top 40 defensive linemen, linebackers or defensive backs, in terms of total fantasy points at their position from 2023 to 2025, or are averaging at least 50 snaps per game, for inclusion in the chart. All defense/special teams are included regardless of whether they meet those minimums. Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Stephen A.: Josh Allen, Bills made a statement with win over Texans (2:09) DJ Bien-Aime Sep 16, 2026, 06:00 AM ET Close DJ Bien-Aime covers the Houston Texans for ESPN. He joined ESPN in July of 2022 after covering the New York Jets for the New York Daily News. He's a former athlete who finished his college career at Louisville. You can catch DJ on ESPN Radio on his show "Talkin' Texans." Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions HOUSTON -- Throughout training camp for the Houston Texans , newly acquired running back David Montgomery was adamant about his all-around ability . In his debut Sunday, he backed his talk -- finishing with the most touchdowns (two rushing and one receiving) in a Texan debut in franchise history. Houston fell short 36-31 to the Buffalo Bills to foil Montgomery's day, but he had 79 total yards (60 rushing and 19 receiving) as Houston scored the most points in a season opener under coach DeMeco Ryans in his four years. Houston had a need at running back, so they traded for Montgomery with the Detroit Lions in March. The offense finished with 124 rushing yards on 32 carries, which helped take pressure off quarterback C.J. Stroud and helped open up passing lanes en route to a 287-yard passing day. "That's going to be our identity," Montgomery said. "[Offensive coordinator] Nick Caley believes in that. Coach Ryans believes in that also. Me, [ Woody Marks ] whenever we get the balls in our hands, we want to make it a point to take it personal to ensure that they can lean on us when they need us." Ryans felt good about the execution from Houston's offensive line combination of left tackle Aireontae Ersery , rookie left guard Keylan Rutledge , center Evan Brown , right guard Ed Ingram and right tackle Trent Brown . If the offensive line can consistently pave running lanes for Montgomery, that'll create the foundation Ryans wants: Physicality. "David doesn't do a great job without talking about the offensive line," Ryans said. "I thought those guys controlled the line of scrimmage really well, especially in those short-yardage, critical situations." From an advanced metrics standpoint, Montgomery's day where he averaged 3.0 yards per carry could have been more efficient all-around. He had a 35% success rate, which ranked 27th among running backs with at least 10 carries in Week 1 according to Next Gen Stats, and Houston's run block win rate was 74% (16th). So there's room to grow. Montgomery called their offensive output "OK" -- which speaks to them not being satisfied. But his individual performance added him to an active two-player list of having a multi-rushing touchdown game with three different franchises ( Detroit Lions , Chicago Bears and Houston) joining his former teammate in quarterback Justin Fields (Bears, Pittsburgh Steelers , New York Jets ). Houston brought in Montgomery with hopes that he could be a true bell cow for an offense that ranked 22nd in rushing yards per game (108.9) and 29th in yards per carry (3.9). "I would've loved to give David a game ball," Ryans said. "Very impressive game by him. Really encouraged with what he brings. Guy who can be an explosive runner, physical runner, he was able to get positive yards -- even when the run may have been blocked for zero [yards], he was able to get four and five yards on runs."

Engineer in a previous incarnation. One time Black Belt. Lover of football, flirter with other sports. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The 2026 NFL season is underway, and Nigerians will once again have plenty of reasons to pay attention, with players of Nigerian origin spread across the league, from defending Super Bowl champions to established starters, and former high draft picks looking for breakout seasons. The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria. There are 137 players of African origin across NFL rosters and practice squads at the start of the 2026 season, representing 24 African countries, with Nigeria accounting for 93 of them, more than two-thirds of the total. Liberia is a distant second with nine players, followed by Côte d'Ivoire with seven, Cameroon with six and Ghana with five. Every NFL team has at least one player of African origin, while Nigerian representation stretches across 29 of the league's 32 teams. Only the Minnesota Vikings , New Orleans Saints and Arizona Cardinals do not have a player of Nigerian origin on their roster or practice squad. No team has more than the New York Jets . The Jets have eight players of Nigerian origin, including one on the practice squad, with Olu Fashanu , Joseph Ossai and Lagos-born veteran David Onyemata among the most recognizable. Those numbers help illustrate how dramatically Nigeria's footprint in American football has grown. The country's NFL connection is no longer represented by a handful of isolated success stories. Nigerian-born players and the children of Nigerian immigrants now occupy positions across the league, from quarterbacks and offensive linemen to linebackers, defensive backs and pass rushers. Some are already champions. Uchenna Nwosu and Nick Emmanwori helped the Seattle Seahawks win Super Bowl LX last season, while Moro Ojomo and Osa Odighizuwa enter this year on NFC teams with legitimate championship ambitions. Foye Oluokun remains one of the league's most productive linebackers, while former high draft picks Olu Fashanu and David Ojabo enter potentially important seasons in their development as potential breakout candidates. Jalen Milroe , whose playing time may be considerably more limited but whose position, Nigerian heritage and presence on the defending champions make his development particularly intriguing. Several others could have a significant say in who is still playing when Super Bowl LXI arrives in Los Angeles on Feb. 14. From the contenders to the challengers and potential breakout players, here are 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch in 2026. SUPER BOWL CONTENDERS Uchenna Nwosu, Edge, Seattle Seahawks There is probably no better place to start than Nwosu. He is an established NFL veteran, a Super Bowl champion and a significant contributor on a Seattle team trying to win consecutive titles. Nwosu played 16 games last season and recorded seven sacks, his best total since registering 9.5 in 2022. He played 33 defensive snaps in Seattle's season-opening 13-10 victory over New England, finishing with five tackles and a pass defended as the Seahawks began their title defense by beating the team they defeated in Super Bowl LX. At 29, Nwosu is entering a stage where another strong season and another championship run would add considerably to an already successful NFL career. Why watch: An established Nigerian-American pass rusher playing significant snaps for the defending champions. Super Bowl chances : Excellent. Nick Emmanwori, Safety, Seattle Seahawks Nwosu may be the established veteran, but Emmanwori could eventually become the bigger star. The young safety made an immediate impact as a rookie, finishing runner-up for AP Defensive Rookie of the Year and helping Seattle win the Super Bowl. At 6-foot-3, Emmanwori possesses unusual size and athleticism for a safety, allowing Seattle to deploy him in multiple roles rather than simply leaving him deep in the secondary. The challenge now is the second season. Opposing offenses have a full year of film on him, while expectations are considerably higher than when he arrived in the league. An offseason ankle problem also makes his health worth monitoring early in the season. If healthy, Emmanwori has an opportunity to establish himself among the league's emerging defensive stars. Why watch: He could make the jump from outstanding rookie to one of the NFL's better young defensive backs. Super Bowl chances: Excellent. Moro Ojomo, DT, Philadelphia Eagles Ojomo has taken a very different route than usual to the NFL. Born in Lagos, he moved to California with his family when he was 8, eventually starred at Texas and was selected by the Philadelphia Eagles in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL draft. For players selected that late, simply sticking around is an achievement. Ojomo has done considerably more. He has developed into an increasingly important part of an Eagles defensive front featuring Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis , giving Philadelphia another source of interior pressure. That development makes 2026 particularly interesting. Ojomo has already gone from seventh-round project to legitimate NFL contributor. Another step Up the ladder could make him a much more recognizable name beyond Philadelphia. Why watch: One of the best development stories among Nigerian-born players in the NFL and now an important piece on a championship contender. Super Bowl chances: Very good. Osa Odighizuwa, DT, San Francisco 49ers There are flashier names on this list, but few have been more dependable. Odighizuwa played all 17 games in each of his final four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys before moving to San Francisco, establishing himself as one of the league's more durable interior defensive linemen. Odighizuwa also comes from a football family. His older brother Owamagbe played in the NFL and now Osa arrives in San Francisco with an obvious assignment. The 49ers recorded an NFL-low 20 sacks last season and needed additional help for a defensive front that had lost some of its previous dominance. Odighizuwa provides an established interior presence alongside Nick Bosa . His first game suggested that the opportunity will be substantial this season. He started at defensive tackle and recorded two tackles as San Francisco's defense overwhelmed the Rams in a 27-7 season-opening victory in Melbourne. They limited the Rams to just seven points and 290 total yards, forced two turnovers, and limited Matthew Stafford to 155 passing yards With fellow starting tackle Alfred Collins lost for the season with a torn patellar tendon, Odighizuwa is now an even more important part of a 49ers defensive front attempting to return to its old standards. Why watch: Proven durability, substantial playing time and a new role on a team expecting to contend. Super Bowl chances: Very good. CHALLENGERS Michael Onwenu, OL, New England Patriots Onwenu already knows how close the Patriots came. New England's 2025 season carried them all the way to Super Bowl LX before Seattle ended the run with a 29-13 victory. Onwenu remains one of New England's most important offensive linemen and has provided valuable versatility throughout his career, playing both guard and tackle. His role becomes even more important with quarterback Drake Maye established as the centerpiece of the Patriots offense. Onwenu began 2026 where he left off, starting at right guard as New England's rebuilt offensive line allowed just two sacks against Seattle in its 13-10 opening-night loss. The Patriots still had problems dealing with Seattle's pressure, particularly late, but Onwenu remains the established presence on an offensive line charged with protecting Maye as New England attempts to return to the Super Bowl. Why watch: An established Nigerian-American starter protecting one of the AFC's leading young quarterbacks. Super Bowl chances: Very good. David Njoku , TE, Los Angeles Chargers Njoku provides something this Nigerian group otherwise lacks: an established offensive skill-position player, having built a substantial NFL career as an athletic receiving tight end and now begins a new chapter with the Los Angeles Chargers. His production dipped last season, when he caught 33 passes for 293 yards and four touchdowns in 12 games, making his fresh start alongside Justin Herbert particularly interesting. Why watch: A proven offensive player getting a fresh start with one of the NFL's established quarterbacks. Super Bowl chances: Good. Foye Oluokun, LB, Jacksonville Jaguars If playing time and production were the only criteria, Oluokun would be much higher. The linebacker has been one of the NFL's most prolific tacklers, including league-leading totals of 192 with Atlanta in 2021 and 184 in his first season with Jacksonville. Oluokun is an established every-down linebacker and a central figure in Jacksonville's defense. Why watch: Perhaps the safest bet among this entire group to accumulate substantial playing time and production. Super Bowl chances: Outside chance. POTENTIAL BREAKOUTS Olu Fashanu, OT, New York Jets The Jets selected Olumuyiwa Fashanu in the first round of the 2024 draft after an outstanding college career at Penn State, viewing the Nigerian-American tackle as a potential long-term cornerstone of their offensive line. Eventually, draft position has to translate into production, and it is about time for that developmental period to give way to expectation. Fashanu possesses the size, footwork and pedigree that made him one of the premier offensive-line prospects in his draft class. Now he needs to establish himself as a high-level NFL starter. Why watch: Former first-round talent approaching a potentially defining stage of his development. Super Bowl chances: It is the Jets... David Ojabo, Edge, Miami Dolphins Few players on this list have a wider range of possible outcomes than Ojabo. Born in Port Harcourt, Ojabo spent part of his childhood in Nigeria before moving to Scotland and eventually the United States. He took up American football relatively late but developed so quickly at Michigan that he was projected as a potential first-round pick before tearing his Achilles at his pro day. Injuries repeatedly interrupted his career in Baltimore, and Miami now provides another opportunity. At 26, there is still time to show that the physical talent which once made him one of college football's most intriguing edge defenders can translate consistently to the NFL. Why watch: This could be a pivotal season for one of the most naturally talented Nigerian-born players in the league. Super Bowl chances: Low. Jalen Milroe, QB, Seattle Seahawks Milroe is the wildcard of this selection. Incidentally, not many are even aware that he has Nigerian heritage, and only a deep dive into his full name, Jalen Oluwaseun Isaiah Milroe, would give it away. His position, as one of only two quarterbacks of Nigerian origin in the league - the other being former Kansas City practice squad QB Chris Oladokun , who is now a free agent - makes his development worth following. Milroe is not Seattle's starting quarterback, meaning he could play considerably fewer snaps than anybody else in this top 10. But he did get minutes last season, and quarterbacks operate under different rules. Milroe's exceptional running ability gives Seattle the possibility of using him in specialized packages, while his longer-term development could eventually determine whether he gets an opportunity to become an NFL starter. Why watch: A quarterback of Nigerian heritage with exceptional physical tools developing on the roster of the NFL champions. Super Bowl chances: Excellent as a member of Seattle, although his individual role could be limited. HONORABLE MENTIONS Boye Mafe , Edge, Cincinnati Bengals : The Nigerian-American pass rusher leaves Seattle with a Super Bowl ring and joins a Cincinnati team capable of making noise in the AFC. Odafe Oweh , Edge, Washington Commanders : Oweh is one of the more physically gifted pass rushers in the league. His cross-town move from Baltimore gives him another opportunity to translate those tools into consistent production. Joseph Ossai, Edge, New York Jets: Lagos-born Ossai has shown disruptive ability without yet producing consistently enough to become a leading NFL edge defender. David Onyemata, DT, New York Jets: Born in Lagos and introduced to organized American football after moving to Canada for university, Onyemata has fashioned a remarkable decade-long NFL career. Olu Oluwatimi , C, Seattle Seahawks: Oluwatimi appeared in eight regular-season games with four starts before playing in all three games of Seattle's postseason championship run. He begins 2026 behind the starters, but could become important if injuries create an opportunity.

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Why nothing went right for the Broncos in Week 1 (0:50) Jeff Legwold Sep 16, 2026, 06:00 AM ET Close Jeff Legwold covers the Denver Broncos at ESPN. He has covered the Broncos for more than 20 years and also assists with NFL draft coverage, joining ESPN in 2013. He has been a member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame Board of Selectors since 1999, too. Jeff previously covered the Pittsburgh Steelers, Buffalo Bills and Houston Oilers/Tennessee Titans at previous stops prior to ESPN. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Stumbling out of the gate has been a theme for the Denver Broncos since Sean Payton was hired as coach prior to the 2023 season. And those slow starts are coming to the forefront again after Monday night's season-opening loss to the Kansas City Chiefs . The 31-10 meltdown at Arrowhead Stadium was the first game of a brutal opening stretch that could potentially put the Broncos in a big hole by mid-October if recent history repeats itself. Denver's next five games are against 2025 playoff teams that won at least 11 games last season. And two opponents in that stretch -- including the Jacksonville Jaguars , who the Broncos (0-1) will play in their home opener on Sunday ( 4:05 p.m. ET, Empower Field at Mile High, CBS ) -- scored 27 or more points in Week 1 victories. "We're kind of tired of these slow starts," said edge rusher Nik Bonitto in a sullen locker room as Monday night turned into Tuesday morning. "Coming out every year and not starting the way we want. I don't think it was a wake-up call; we've just got to execute better from everybody." Monday's loss dropped the Broncos to 4-8 in September under Payton. They've won only one of their past four openers and are trying to avoid their third 0-2 start in four seasons. Even last season, when Denver went 14-3 and advanced to the AFC Championship Game, started with two losses in the first three weeks. So, starting faster was a talking point throughout August, both publicly and behind the scenes. "I don't think we've really started fast here in my three years -- I'm pretty sure we haven't," Payton said just before the season began. "... I think that's going to be important." It could be vitally important to the Broncos' playoff pursuits given how frontloaded their schedule is this season. Next up are the Jaguars (1-0), who got four touchdown passes from Trevor Lawrence in their season-opening win over the Cleveland Browns . Jacksonville won the AFC South with a 13-4 record last season, which included a 34-20 victory in Denver last December that snapped an 11-game Broncos winning streak. That will be followed by a Sunday night home game against the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams (0-1). Then the Broncos will hit the road to play the San Francisco 49ers (1-0) and Los Angeles Chargers (0-1). The tough stretch finishes with a short-week, Thursday night game at home against the Seattle Seahawks (1-0). The schedule softens considerably after that point, as the Broncos face only one opponent that finished last season with a winning record in Weeks 7-15. But they know they can't afford to dig a massive hole before that. "I think everybody knows [Payton] has talked about a fast start," Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton said. "You go into every game thinking you want to get going early and you don't really think about anything more than the week in front of you. So, it's just like, if we start fast each week that's a fast start of a season." Monday's loss was particularly troubling, especially the run defense and quarterback Bo Nix 's unsettled play in Davis Webb's first regular-season game as the playcaller. Nix was sacked four times for only the second time in his three-year career. He fumbled three times (losing one) and threw an interception, finishing 17-of-28 with 131 passing yards with a touchdown and the interception. The Broncos gained only 176 total yards on a mere 47 plays (32 pass plays, 15 runs), with Payton saying the Broncos' game plan had "a lot of throws, not enough runs." The leaky run defense is a growing issue, as Monday was the third consecutive game (including playoffs) the Broncos had given up at least 141 rushing yards dating to last season. The Chiefs pounded out 220 rushing yards, 173 coming from running back Kenneth Walker III . Kansas City pointed its rushing plays toward the middle of the formation, often pinning linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad away from ball carriers. The Chiefs broke 19 tackles Monday, according to ESPN Research, with Walker breaking 11. The Broncos broke six as a team . "Coach had us in the right spot and we missed tackles and plays we were in the wrong spot," Singleton said. "... We're going to point the fingers at ourselves." Monday wasn't the fast start the Broncos hoped for, but they can take solace in being able to dig out of slow starts the past two seasons to make the playoffs. Denver started 0-2 in 2024 and was 5-5 in November before finishing on a 5-2 kick to reach the postseason. Last season's 1-2 start was erased by 13 wins in the Broncos' final 14 regular-season games. Even in 2023, when the Broncos' 0-3 start included an infamous 70-20 loss to the Miami Dolphins , Denver recovered and had a 6-5 record entering December before finishing 8-9. But that all seemed like ancient history as the Broncos quietly packed their gear to leave Arrowhead. Now they must find solutions on the practice field the rest of the week before they face the Jaguars in Game No. 2 of a rough six-week opening stretch. "We know this is not going to be the whole season for us," Nix said. "That's the first time since Baltimore [a 41-10 loss in Week 9 in 2024] that we've been beat pretty handily like that. ... I do think [Monday] was not a good representation of us as a team."

Paye - a Guinea-born Liberian defensive end - earns our Africa player of the Week nod for the first week of the new NFL season. There were plenty of other stars - either from the continent directly or with directly traceable lineage - who started with a bang. Kyle Monangai - a first-generation Cameroonian-American running back - scored a memorable touchdown for the Chicago Bears in their win over the Carolina Panthers . Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who is of Sierra Leonean descent through his grandparents - gave a timely reminder of why he is the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year in the Seattle Seahawks ' win over the New England Patriots . Africa Player of the Week: Kwity Paye (Las Vegas Raiders) Paye was involved in three of the five sacks on Malik Willis in his first regular season game for the Raiders after joining from the Indianapolis Colts - ending with a personal tally of two (one sack and two split-sacks, counting for 0.5 each). He additionally notched four quarter-back hits among a total of six tackles. The 27-year-old played an integral part in a solid defensive performance as the Raiders beat the Miami Dolphins 27-13. Paye pinned the Dolphins back two yards with his very first tackle of the game on the first drive - made together with Taron Johnson on De'Von Achane . His first split-sack came on the second Dolphins drive as he and Folorunso Fatukasi - who is of Nigerian descent - brought down Willis. Paye picked up another split-sack on Willis with Maxx Crosby early in the fourth quarter to keep the lead at 14 points. The last sack of the game on Willis - with around three minutes remaining - was all Paye's and by that stage, it was effectively the cherry on the icing, topping off a tremendous debut. Africa Moment of the Week: Kyle Monangai (Chicago Bears) Monangai scored a career best 61-yard running touchdown in the Bears' 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers. While the Bears may eventually have won the game by a comfortable 22-point margin, the victory was far from settled at the time of Monangai's marauding run, which stretched the lead from seven to 14 points at the end of the third quarter. Monangai's Cameroonian parents grew up loving soccer, but in his second season in the NFL, their son continues to excel at a different type of football. Honorable Mentions Jaxon Smith-Njigba gained 122 yards across eight receptions in the Seattle Seahawks' 13-10 win over the New England Patriots, picking up where he left off last season and scoring a touchdown. Boye Mafe , the proud son of Nigerian parents, brought down Baker Mayfield and forced a fumble in the Cincinnati Bengals ' 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Foyesade Oluokun , another star with ties to Nigeria, made an interception in the Jacksonville Jaguars ' 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns . Another compatriot, Kingsley Enagbare , made a sack in the New York Jets ' 23-10 over the Tennessee Titans . Elic Ayomanor , who is of Nigerian and Liberian descent, was on the losing side despite scoring a touchdown. play 1:03 Bruschi, Rex marvel at Bears after big offensive game in Week 1 Chuba Hubbard , like Ayomanor, is Canadian and of Nigerian descent. He, too, was on the scoreboard in a defeat in Week 1. Hubbard scored two touchdowns in the Panthers' defeat to the Bears. Bobby Okereke - a California-born star of proud Nigerian heritage forced a fumble despite ending up on the losing side. Nigeria-born Princely Umanmielen picked up a sack for the Panthers in defeat. Odafe Oweh (a first-generation American of Nigerian descent and a Washington Commanders star) made a sack in the narrow 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . Donovan Ezeiruaku - also of Nigerian descent - had an impressive performance on defense for the Dallas Cowboys but also ended up on the losing side in a 28-20 defeat to the New York Giants . Felix Anudike-Uzomah - yet another player with roots in Nigeria - made a sack for the Kansas City Chiefs in their 31-10 Monday night win over the Denver Broncos . Africa-born Player Watch The obvious winner among players born on the continent is Paye this week as he claims Africa Player of the Week honors even ahead of those from the diaspora not born directly in Africa. It is not every week that the continent gets to see a performance as spectacular as Paye's, but Africa has undoubtedly advanced in the development of homegrown talent. Paye's heroics and Umanmielen's sack for the Panthers aside, Zimbabwe's Nate Landman made eight tackles in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , though he was injured in the process. Landman will hope to be fit for the clash against the Giants - who gave homegrown Nigerian International Player Pathway (IPP) star Basil Chijioke 'CJ' Okoye his team debut in the 28-20 win over the Cowboys.

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Nick Wagoner Sep 15, 2026, 06:00 PM ET Close Nick Wagoner is an NFL reporter at ESPN. Nick has covered the San Francisco 49ers since 2016, having previously covered the St. Louis Rams for 12 years, including three years (2013 to 2015) at ESPN. In over a decade with the company, Nick has led ESPN's coverage of the Niners' 2019 and 2023 Super Bowl run, Colin Kaepernick's protest, the Rams making Michael Sam the first openly gay player drafted to the NFL, Sam's subsequent pursuit of a roster spot and the team's relocation and stadium saga. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions MELBOURNE, Australia -- More than halfway through the second quarter of Thursday's win over the Los Angeles Rams , San Francisco 49ers center Jake Brendel could feel things turning in his team's direction. The Niners were midway through an 86-yard scoring drive, and rookie running back Kaelon Black had just ripped off gains of 9 and 5 yards. From midfield, Brendel turned toward coach Kyle Shanahan on the sideline and waved his arms to suggest he wanted to run the ball, run it again and keep running it until the Rams showed they could at least slow it down. "After a few of those good chunk run plays hit, I'm looking right at Kyle, 'Let's go,'" Brendel said. "Let's just keep going. Let's keep dialing them up." Shanahan apparently agreed with Brendel's assessment. The success of those plays only yielded more runs, and by the end of San Francisco's 27-7 win, it had 30 attempts for a robust 5.8 yards per rush. That would've been the team's second-best outing for the 2025 season (behind its 5.9 against the Bears in Week 17 ). Perhaps more important was how the 49ers got back to their bread and butter. Since trading for Christian McCaffrey in October 2022, Shanahan has explored finding a legitimate complement to the team's RB1 before either eschewing the idea completely or giving up after potential options failed to produce. Though the Niners only have a one-game sample size, the early returns indicate that Black might be the powerful complement they've long sought next to McCaffrey. "I thought they both ran really hard and really well," Shanahan said. "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more." When McCaffrey is healthy, balance has not been the word anyone would use to describe the 49ers' distribution of carries. The Melbourne game marked the first time a Niner had more rushing attempts (Black had 14) than McCaffrey (10) in a game he started and finished since the 2022 divisional playoffs against the Dallas Cowboys . Black had only one reception compared to McCaffrey's four, but that left them with an even split of 15 touches each for 70 and 88 yards, respectively. Black's extensive snaps came as a result of design and a bit because of McCaffrey dealing with cramps during the game, but Black earning such a role after missing a chunk of training camp with an adductor injury speaks volumes for the 24-year-old third-round pick. Especially given the 49ers' recent history of draft misses at the position in the middle rounds. "[Black is] a force and he's someone who's going to help our team a whole lot," McCaffrey said. "It was really cool to see him go out there and just do what he does." Equally encouraging for the 49ers was that the 1-2 punch got off to a strong start after a disappointing 2025 season on the ground. Last season, the 49ers averaged just 3.8 yards per carry (30th in the NFL), 106.9 yards per game (24th) and 2.04 yards before contact per carry (29th). The yards per carry and yards before contact marks were the worst in a single season since Shanahan took over in 2017 -- and that was with McCaffrey for all 17 games. In addition to a more balanced attack, the 49ers also showed creativity with their play design under new run game coordinator Joe Graves. San Francisco threw a variety of motions, including some that allowed fullback Kyle Juszczyk to lead block for McCaffrey or Black. The 49ers motioned players on 59% of their offensive plays, the highest rate in any game under Shanahan. They averaged 6.3 yards per rush on 20 attempts using any form of motion. San Francisco also took advantage of a schematic curveball from the Rams. According to Brendel, the Niners spent the week preparing for plenty of five-man fronts -- similar to what Los Angeles threw at them in recent matchups. Brendel was surprised when the Rams not only played four down linemen more frequently but were also often in nickel packages (five defensive backs). On 16 attempts against four or fewer man fronts, the Niners averaged 6.6 yards per attempt. Against nickel and dime (six DBs) looks, San Francisco averaged 6.5 yards per carry . "The way that they chose to play us on defense schematically we weren't really expecting," Brendel said. "Most teams are a little bit more scared of our wide zone and our run game." As the 49ers continued having rushing success in Melbourne, the offensive line could sense an opportunity to impose its will. In the third quarter, the team averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the road-weary Rams. It was the perfect storm for what the 49ers hope is a reestablishment of their previous levels of dominance on the ground. "We felt it from the jump," right tackle Colton McKivitz said. "I definitely think our plan helped us being down here a week and getting our legs. ... We were kind of called out last year for not being a good running team. And this is a good start for us. "Obviously, it's Week 1 ... but when you can start with that number of rushing yards against a good defensive front, against a rival, it shows we're going in the right direction."
