Follow on X Multiple Authors Sep 14, 2026, 11:26 PM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Back on the field inside Arrowhead Stadium for the first time in nine months, quarterback Patrick Mahomes wasn't the biggest star -- or the biggest difference-maker -- in the Kansas City Chiefs ' resounding 31-10 win Monday night over the AFC West rival Denver Broncos . Running back Kenneth Walker III , the reigning Super Bowl MVP who joined the Chiefs in March, was stellar in his Kansas City debut. Monday's outcome was exactly what the Chiefs wanted from their offense, as Walker's speed and ball-carrying abilities took much of the burden off Mahomes, who made his much-anticipated return from the surgery that repaired the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, an injury that occurred Dec. 14. In 26 touches, in a variety of ways, Walker ran through, around and past the Broncos for an outstanding performance, finishing with 191 all-purpose yards and two touchdowns. Walker converted on four short-yardage situations, including a 60-yard touchdown on fourth-and-inches early in the third quarter. He became just the third player since 2000 with least 100 rushing yards in his Chiefs debut, joining running back Kareem Hunt (148 yards in 2017) and Clyde Edwards-Helaire (138 yards in 2020), according to ESPN Research. The Broncos never led and were never able to get quarterback Bo Nix into rhythm. Nix, who also was returning after having two offseason surgeries to repair his fractured right ankle -- which forced him to miss last season's AFC Championship Game -- struggled throughout, including throwing an interception on the Broncos' opening drive. The Chiefs sacked Nix four times, and speedy receiver Jaylen Waddle , one of Denver's biggest offseason acquisitions, was limited to just one reception for 2 yards. Here are the most important things to know for both teams: Kansas City Chiefs What to make of the QB performance: Mahomes wasn't perfect, but he didn't need to be to beat the Broncos. The Chiefs' opening drive demonstrated Mahomes' toughness and impressive speed when he scrambled out of the pocket inside the red zone to score a 15-yard touchdown. Mahomes' top speed on his highlight was 15.8 mph, which was 2.5 mph faster than his average speed on rushing attempts last season, according to Next Gen Stats. In the second half, Mahomes improved his passing rhythm to finish with 184 yards and two touchdown passes. Most surprising performance: The Chiefs' defense dominated the Broncos, doing so with the help of an influx of rookies. Cornerback Mansoor Delane , the sixth pick, intercepted Nix to set up the Chiefs' first touchdown. Defensive end R Mason Thomas finished with a sack, and defensive tackle Peter Woods generated pressure on passing downs. Even cornerback Nohl Williams , a second-year player, did an excellent job in coverage against receiver Courtland Sutton , who finished with just two receptions for 11 yards. -- Nate Taylor Next game: vs. Indianapolis Colts (Sunday, Sept. 20, at 8:20 p.m. ET) Denver Broncos The Broncos spent an offseason outlining just how much they needed an improved run game and new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. And then they spent their opening night of the season with little action from either. Denver ran the ball just 12 times in the game. Waddle, who did show his potential impact on Evan Engram's touchdown catch in the first quarter when several Chiefs defenders leaned toward Waddle as Engram ran free, had one catch for 2 yards when the game was still in the balance. This was not the debut the Broncos wanted. They're still searching for that improved run game -- and for Waddle to be a big part of the offense. Most surprising performance: On a night the Broncos held Mahomes to 15-of-27 passing, Walker did the most damage. He romped for a 60-yard touchdown on Kansas City's fourth play of the second half, giving him 149 yards to that point, leaving a pile of missed tackles in his wake. Walker finished with 173 yards to go with a rushing TD and a receiving TD, more rushing yards than any back had against the Broncos in all of 2025. What to make of the QB performance: Nix showed some quick bounce-back ability early. After he took a sack and threw an interception in the first and third plays from scrimmage, respectively, he went 5-for-5 on a touchdown drive in the Broncos' next possession. But overall, he, like the rest of the Broncos' offense, looked out of sorts. Nix fumbled three times, losing one, and threw an interception. It was just the third lost fumble for Nix in his career, with one of those being in last season's opener. Trend to watch: Running back J.K. Dobbins was one of the league's rushing leaders when he suffered a season-ending foot injury in a Week 10 win over the Raiders last November. Coach Sean Payton said re-signing Dobbins in the offseason was one of the team's highest priorities because the Broncos had big plans for the 27-year-old back. One game does not a season make, but in offensive coordinator Davis Webb's first regular-season game as a playcaller, Dobbins had just three carries in the first half and the Broncos were down two scores before Dobbins got carries on consecutive plays. Stat of note: While Payton has called Nix's ability to be "hard to sack'' one of the quarterback's superpowers, the Chiefs sacked Nix four times Monday. Nix was sacked more than twice in only two games last season -- three by the Raiders and four by the Chargers in the regular-season finale. -- Jeff Legwold Next game: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (Sunday, Sept. 20, at 4:05 p.m. ET)

title: Walker runs all over Denver, Mahomes looks healthy as Chiefs beat up Broncos 31-10

new_body: Chiefs 31-10 Broncos (Sep 14, 2026) Game Recap - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Denver Broncos @ Kansas City Chiefs Denver Broncos Broncos DEN 0-1 , 0-1 Away 10 0-1 , 0-1 Away Final 1 2 3 4 T Broncos DEN 7 0 3 0 10 Chiefs KC 7 7 10 7 31 Kansas City Chiefs Chiefs KC 1-0 , 1-0 Home 31 1-0 , 1-0 Home By AP Updated: Sep 15, 2026, 12:25 am Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — So many people seemed to be focused on Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes , and how the two-time MVP's surgically repaired left knee would hold up in Kansas City's season opener against the Broncos, that they forgot all about Kenneth Walker III . The reigning Super Bowl MVP won't be surprising anyone else anytime soon. Walker ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns in his Chiefs debut , helping to take some of the pressure off Mahomes in his first game back, and Kansas City exacted some revenge on Denver for stealing its AFC West crown with a 31-10 victory Monday night. Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star also had three catches for 18 yards. “He did a really nice job,” Reid said, “and you never know going in how many times you're going to give him the ball. That's not a calculated thing. You have to be making yards. For him to play the way he did I thought was spectacular.” Mahomes wasn't a slouch, either. With a brace protecting his left knee , he threw for 184 yards and two scores while also running for another score, helping the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as division champs. “They were in the AFC championship game for a reason,” Mahomes said. “For us to go out and win like that, that's the first step. It shows all the work in training camp paid off. But how can we be better?” Good question. The Chiefs helped to make Denver positively abysmal on offense in its first game with coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays . Bo Nix threw for 131 yards with an interception and a lost fumble, and the Broncos finished with 176 yards of offense, all despite the offseason splash they made by trading a package of draft picks to Miami for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle . Waddle had one catch for 2 yards. Evan Engram led the Broncos with four catches for 43 yards and their lone TD. “As a whole offense, a whole team, we just didn’t play really good,” Nix said. “Obviously not a good evening," Broncos coach Sean Payton added. The looming question, even after Mahomes participated in the entire offseason program and every practice of training camp, was how his knee would hold up nine months to the day since he was hurt in a game against the Chargers. He erased any doubts when he capped the Chiefs' opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run. “Once you put him in the game,” Reid said, “he's going to play, and you better be confident in that.” It was Walker who did most of the running, though. The Super Bowl MVP for Seattle, who signed a three-year, $43.05 million deal in free agency, had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half alone, along with a couple of catches out of the backfield. Even when the Broncos tied the game on Nix's 19-yard touchdown pass to Engram, Walker assumed a heavy load as the Chiefs pieced together a 10-play, 80-yard drive late in the half. It ended when Mahomes found Rashee Rice , fresh off a knee injury of his own, and he caromed off a couple of Broncos defenders and into the end zone to make it 14-7 at the break. Then it was Walker's turn to bounce off a defender, turning a fourth-and-1 carry into a 60-yard TD run to start the third quarter. “I knew they were going to crash in. When they crashed in, I bounced out,” Walker said, “and I was off to the races from there.” The teams traded field goals later in the quarter thanks to big plays by each side: Brandon Jones picked off Mahomes deep in Chiefs territory, setting up Wil Lutz 's chip shot, and Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 59 yards to set up Harrison Butker 's answer. Nix's fumble on the ensuing possession allowed the Chiefs to put the game away. Mahomes hit rookie running back Emmett Johnson on third down for a 26-yard gain, setting up first-and-goal at the Denver 2. And in the kind of creative — dare say, fun? — play that was reminiscent of the Chiefs' banner years, Mahomes lined up in a three-point stance alongside backup QB Justin Fields , took the snap and shoveled the ball to Walker, who scooted untouched for the score. It was a play that Reid and his staff found in some black-and-white footage from the 1930s, and it worked flawlessly. “It was hard to see,” Walker said of the film, “but we worked it over and over in practice. We felt it was going to work and it did.” Arrowhead over Emmys Taylor Swift chose Arrowhead Stadium over the Emmy Awards to cheer on Kelce. The pop star married the Chiefs tight end on July 3. Swift, who watched alongside Tom Cruise, had been nominated for outstanding variety special (pre-recorded) for “The Eras Tour: The Final Show,” but the category winner — “The Muppet Show” — had been announced earlier this month. Injuries Broncos: WR Marvin Mims left briefly with a hip injury but returned. Chiefs: CB Mansoor Delane landed on his right shoulder after an interception on the third play of the game. The No. 6 pick in the NFL draft was helped to the locker room and did not return. ... LB Cooper McDonald (knee) left in the first half and did not return. Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Schefter: Drew Brees mulled NFL return for Broncos in AFC title game (1:27) Adam Schefter Sep 14, 2026, 07:37 PM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions It turns out that Philip Rivers' out-of-nowhere return to the NFL last season almost started a trend that would have been trumped by the potential return of Drew Brees. After the Denver Broncos lost starting quarterback Bo Nix to a fractured ankle in their overtime playoff victory against the Buffalo Bills , Denver's then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael had discussions with Brees about the former star quarterback coming out of retirement to be ready for the AFC Championship Game, sources told ESPN. Brees had turned 47 years old just two days before Nix sustained the ankle injury Jan. 17. Brees spoke to Lombardi and Carmichael, his longtime assistant coaches with the New Orleans Saints , early in the week ahead of Denver's AFC Championship Game showdown against the New England Patriots , telling them that he wanted to first work out to see how his body would respond. But once he tried, Brees found discomfort in his wrist and nixed the idea that would have become one of the most improbable returns in NFL history, according to sources. Brees hinted earlier this year at a potential opportunity to return to the NFL, telling the "New Heights" podcast that he "had some conversations." In an interview published Feb. 11, Brees told "New Heights" that "something happened where I thought there might be a chance where I could play that week." Brees did not identify a specific team or provide details on the situation he was alluding to, but acknowledged that he was "not there" in terms of being physically able to play. Brees announced his retirement in March 2021, 15 years to the day that he first signed with the Saints, and was selected for induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame this past summer. There are bylaws that say players must wait five years after their playing careers are concluded to be inducted into the Hall of Fame, and it's fair to wonder how the Hall would have handled this unprecedented situation and if the clock to entry into Canton would have been restarted. It's also fair to wonder how Broncos head coach Sean Payton -- Brees' longtime head coach in New Orleans -- would have handled Brees' return. Lombardi and Carmichael did not include Payton or inform him about their initial conversations with Brees. The assistant coaches first wanted to see if Brees was willing to return to the NFL to help Denver try to reach the Super Bowl before informing Payton. Payton only heard about the behind-the-scenes plot in the offseason, according to sources. When he did, Payton thought his assistants were referring to a potential Brees return for a Monday night game vs. Miami in December 2021, when the Saints lost quarterback Jameis Winston to a torn ACL, had Taysom Hill and Trevor Siemian put on the reserve/COVID-19 list, and were forced to have rookie quarterback Ian Book make his NFL debut. Back then, Payton and his assistants approached Brees about returning to the Saints, and he debated the idea before ultimately nixing it, according to sources. But Payton spearheaded that attempt, whereas in the more recent discussions that occurred this past January, he didn't know about them. When Payton found out that his assistants had broached the idea of a Brees return for the AFC Championship Game during the offseason, he was fascinated and flabbergasted. Had Brees decided his body felt good enough to return, Payton and the Broncos would have signed him and figured out whether he was a better starting quarterback option than Jarrett Stidham . As one Broncos source recently said: "At a minimum, you sign [Brees], he's 1A or 1B. And Drew's point was: 'I know how to win a game like that.'" Payton was asked Monday night, after the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs , about what the potential was for Brees to join Denver. Payton said Lombardi and Carmichael had talked to Brees without his knowledge and never brought the idea to him. "I just know I was the odd man out. I never heard anything about it,'' Payton said Monday night. "It never came to anything, I was only told about it later. I was just like you guys.'' With Stidham as their starter, the Broncos lost 10-7 to the Patriots in Denver. Stidham struggled in the snowy contest, completing 17 of 31 passes for 133 yards, one touchdown and one interception while also losing a fumble. Certainly, Brees and Payton have been close enough, and could have made a comeback work. The two discussed it this past summer, when Payton presented Brees for induction at the Pro Football Hall of Fame. The two men, as instrumental as any in the history of New Orleans football, could have had the chance to write another wilder chapter in Denver. ESPN's Jeff Legwold contributed to this report.

He joined ESPN in September 2019 as an NBA reporter dedicated to the Midwest region before switching to his current role in April 2021. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- Detroit Lions running back Isiah Pacheco will "miss a significant amount of time" after recently undergoing surgery to remove a loose body that was pressing on a nerve in his back, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Pacheco could return in early December with the recovery process expected to take about 12 weeks. The procedure was performed by Dr. Robert Watkins IV, who is respected as one of the nation's experts. "It's going to be a while," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said of Pacheco's timetable for recovery. "I really can't. It'll be a significant amount of time though." Pacheco was already slated to miss Detroit's first four games after being placed on the injured reserve list with a designation to return back on Sept. 1 while dealing with an MCL sprain and the back injury, both of which he suffered during training camp. The Lions added Pacheco this offseason as a free agent to pair with star running back Jahmyr Gibbs after trading veteran running back David Montgomery to the Houston Texans . He spent his first four seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs , where he won two Super Bowl titles. Lions starting left guard Christian Mahogany 's status for Thursday night's matchup against the Buffalo Bills is in question after he suffered a hip injury and was carted to the locker room during the first half of Sunday's win over the New Orleans Saints . Campbell doesn't feel like Mahogany's injury is will be a long-term deal, but did say "it could be tough to get him ready" for the short turnaround and trip to Buffalo.

Archer has covered the NFL since 1997 and Dallas since 2003. He joined ESPN in 2010. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys will likely be without a starting linebacker and key contributor at safety for the next two games, according to coach Brian Schottenheimer. DeMarvion Overshown , who handled the coach-to-player communication as the middle linebacker, could miss one to two weeks with a hamstring strain that knocked him out of the second half of Sunday's season-opening loss against the New York Giants . Safety Malik Hooker is scheduled to undergo surgery on a fractured forearm, but he will not go on injured reserve, which would knock him out for at least four games. "It sounds like it's one that doesn't require as long of a period of time," Schottenheimer said Monday, "so we're hoping it's a two-week window." Schottenheimer indicated they will keep Caleb Downs in his role as a safety and slot player in passing situations, with P.J. Locke taking over the snaps Hooker would see in the sub package. "Caleb's a guy that can move around, but we like him down near the line of scrimmage," Schottenheimer said. Replacing Overshown is a little trickier. The Cowboys mostly went with rookie Jaishawn Barham next to Dee Winters but mixed in Shemar James for a handful of snaps. "We've got to move these guys around a little bit," Schottenheimer said. "Dee Winters is obviously most experienced of the group. Jaishawn got some valuable playtime [Sunday], did some good things, did some things that he needs to improve on. Shemar James is a valued member of our football team, very smart, very bright. And then obviously we've got some guys on practice squad that we've got elevations. Curtis Robinson is a veteran. He's played a lot of football in this league as well. And then Justin Barron 's a guy we have a lot of high expectations for." It was an inauspicious debut for the Cowboys defensively under first-time coordinator Christian Parker, giving up 28 points, 394 yards and forcing just one punt. The Giants ran for 165 yards and converted 9-of-11 third-down tries, which limited the Cowboys' offense to just two second-half possessions. "I have no question Christian Parker is the right guy for this job. He's an outstanding coach," Schottenheimer said. "He will learn from this, just like our young players are going to learn from this. We're going to play our young players this weekend too, and they're going to play better, and Christian's going to call a better game this week and feel better about it."

Kris covers the Los Angeles Chargers, including coach Jim Harbaugh's franchise-altering first season. In Kris' free time, he lives his NBA dreams at men's leagues across Los Angeles. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that wide receiver Ladd McConkey has a rib injury and is considered day-to-day. McConkey was perhaps the lone bright spot on an ugly day for the Chargers' offense in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals . He had five catches for 82 yards and looked like he could have done much more. But in the third quarter, linebacker Mack Wilson Sr . delivered a big hit as McConkey attempted to make a leaping grab on an in-breaking route in the middle of the field. McConkey lay on the ground in apparent significant pain before exiting. He didn't return. "Ladd's a really good football player," quarterback Justin Herbert said after the game. "We're really glad to have him, and he made a ton of plays today, so I'm hoping he feels better." The Chargers trailed by only two points when McConkey left the game, but the offense spiraled and failed to score after his exit. The four remaining drives were riddled with penalties, and Herbert was sacked two times for a total of three on the day. Harbaugh also said that safety Elijah Molden (hamstring) and wide receiver Derius Davis (undisclosed) are day-to-day. He added that wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith has a hamstring injury and will miss some time. With three receivers potentially set to miss time, this could be an opportunity for fourth-round rookie Brenen Thompson , who had a standout training camp. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel begged general manager Joe Hortiz to select Thompson, telling Hortiz on draft night he'd take his shirt off if the Chargers got him . Thompson was the fastest receiver at the NFL scouting combine with a 4.26 40-yard dash and led the SEC in receiving yards (1,054) at Mississippi State last season. Thompson played just 10 offense snaps Sunday. He wasn't targeted.

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Anthony Gharib Sep 14, 2026, 05:55 PM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The summer of New York is gaining strength in its late stages. The New York Giants and New York Jets both won their Week 1 matchups Sunday. The Giants defeated the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on "Sunday Night Football," and the Jets beat the Tennessee Titans 23-10 earlier in the day. Victories for both of New York's NFL teams in Week 1 are a rare sight. This is the first time the Giants and Jets have each started a campaign 1-0 since 2009, according to ESPN Research. It's also the first time they've both been above .500 at any point of a season since Week 14 in 2022. New York, New York: this is the first time the Giants and Jets both opened 1-0 since 2009, when their head coaches were Tom Coughlin and Rex Ryan. pic.twitter.com/yGBcZ9Uwg9 Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 14, 2026 The other team in New York, the Buffalo Bills , won its opener as well, defeating the Houston Texans 36-31 . That makes all three teams undefeated in Week 1 for the first time since 2008. A hot start for the two current MetLife Stadium tenants brought opposite outcomes in 2009. Two seasons after a Super Bowl victory, the Giants began 5-0 in their final season at Giant Stadium. They then lost four straight games and split wins and losses from Week 11 to 16. The final defeat coincided with a Cowboys win that eliminated the Giants from playoff contention for the first time since 2004. Rex Ryan began his first season as Jets head coach in 2009, and two months in, it looked like the Jets might have to find a new leader. They had a 4-6 record after a 3-0 start to the year. It would mark their worst stretch of the season as the Jets won five of their next six games to reach the playoffs. New York would beat the Cincinnati Bengals in the AFC wild-card round. The Jets then took down No. 2-seeded Los Angeles Chargers in the divisional round to reach the conference championship game for the first time since 1998. The No. 1-seeded Indianapolis Colts ended the Jets' run, but New York would be back in the conference final the following season. It hasn't made the playoffs since. Week 2 pits the Jets and Giants against two NFC teams. The Jets host the Green Bay Packers , while the Giants visit the Los Angeles Rams on "Monday Night Football" (8:15 ET on ABC/ESPN). Regardless of the outcomes, Jets and Giants fans will always be able to brag about Week 1.

Raanan joined ESPN in 2016. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants standout wide receiver Malik Nabers revealed after Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys that head coach John Harbaugh tackled him during a walk-through earlier in the day. It was Harbaugh's way of making light of the final hurdle Nabers faced before returning from a torn ACL suffered last year. "It just kind of evolved into an opportunity to tackle. And I couldn't pass it up, I guess," Harbaugh said with a smile Monday. "It was good. It was fun. It was all in fun. Lot of laughs. Some guys gave me a sideways look, some of the players, like, 'What are you doing?!" It was good." It was not the first time that Harbaugh has applied such a tactic. It seems this was part of the repertoire at some point during his 18-season tenure with the Baltimore Ravens . The Giants hired Harbaugh as their head coach earlier this year. "I may have to add it in. I do tackle guys -- or imitate tackling guys, because I couldn't really tackle them in real life, I'm sure," he said. "I have done that before. So it wasn't a first." Nabers was in good spirits and said he was "feeling good" after Sunday night's win . He caught six passes on nine targets for 69 yards in his first game action since last September. The third-year receiver ultimately made a last-minute decision to play less than two hours before kickoff. Perhaps the simulated tackle from Harbaugh played into the decision. "I knew everyone was worried about if I get tackled and stuff like that," Nabers said after the game. "Actually, Coach Harbaugh tackled me in practice. He tackled me. He wanted to see if I could take a tackle, and he was good. ... [It happened] in walk-through." Not surprisingly, the 63-year-old coach didn't take his No. 1 wide receiver to the ground. "Nah, I didn't go down," Nabers said with a laugh. The whole situation caught the Giants by surprise. They have been extremely cautious with the Nabers situation after a long rehab that included some setbacks. The explosive wide receiver even wore a red no-contact jersey at practice during part of the summer. The Giants left the final decision on whether Nabers would play up to the young receiver. So it was shocking when they saw what happened when Harbaugh approached Nabers during their Sunday walk-through. "Yeah, we were all just chilling on the sideline. It was right before we were supposed to start our walk-through, and things were just up in the air [with Nabers playing]," quarterback Jaxson Dart said. "We didn't know exactly what was going to happen. And me and Coach [Harbaugh] kind of had some conversations. He's like, 'You know what, like, I think that once he gets hit for the first time and realizes that he's OK, then he's going to feel confident.' "So I think in his mind that triggered, 'Oh, maybe I should tackle him right then and there.' So, we're all just standing there, and then all of a sudden, [Nabers] goes down on the ground, and our team's super protective of him. So we all turned to look, and it's Coach [Harbaugh] tackling [Nabers], and then he pops up and he goes, 'See, you're all good.'" Harbaugh said Monday afternoon that the Giants made it through the game fine on the injury front. Nabers has an extra day to get his body ready for a matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on "Monday Night Football."

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that star tight end Brock Bowers is day-to-day after missing the team's Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins because of a meniscus trim procedure he had last week. "[Bowers is] working his tail off to get back out on the field," Kubiak said ahead of the team's Week 2 matchup against the Chargers in Los Angeles on Sunday. "It's really important to him to play as soon as possible, and that doesn't surprise me about Brock." Kubiak said the team will be smart with Bowers and listen to the athletic trainers, including wellness coordinator Alex Guerrero. "If he's ready to play, he's going to play," Kubiak added. Bowers got banged up during training camp, but the injury was diagnosed last week, prompting him to have surgery Dr. Daniel Cooper. Kubiak said he doesn't recall the exact day the injury occurred. Bowers has been dealing with knee issues since last season. He played three games while dealing with a posterior cruciate ligament injury and a bone bruise in his left knee that he suffered in the Raiders' season-opening win over the New England Patriots . He then was sidelined for three games to recover. With Bowers missing from the Raiders' 27-13 win over Miami, Michael Mayer filled the role of TE1 and caught six passes for 32 yards on seven targets.

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Schefter to McAfee: Steelers, Joey Porter Jr. in a tricky spot with contract talks (2:00) Brooke Pryor Sep 14, 2026, 04:37 PM ET Close Brooke Pryor is a reporter for NFL Nation at ESPN who has covered the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. She previously covered the Kansas City Chiefs for the Kansas City Star and the University of Oklahoma for The Oklahoman. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions PITTSBURGH -- A day after opting to hold Joey Porter Jr . out of the season-opening win against the Atlanta Falcons , Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy was noncommittal on the cornerback's timeline to return to game action. Asked if Porter, who missed training camp with a back injury he aggravated during a mobility workout on report day, would need more than this week to complete his "ramp-up" period, McCarthy said the plan was to increase Porter's workload beginning with Wednesday's practice. "Hopefully we'll have a good plan for him on Wednesday, and hopefully we'll do more," McCarthy said Monday. "That's the outlook. So yeah, hopefully we move forward with more volume of work. That would be my anticipation." Once the ramp-up period is over, McCarthy said, he expects Porter to play. Porter's next opportunity to get on the field is Sunday afternoon at Gillette Stadium against the New England Patriots . Porter, 26, has been embroiled in a contentious contract negotiation throughout the offseason, and it ended with the two sides not reaching a deal by the Steelers' regular-season negotiating deadline. The possibility of a trade lingers -- as does using the franchise tag on Porter before he reaches free agency next offseason -- but the Steelers have neither made nor received trade calls on the 2023 second-round pick. Porter was on the sideline for Sunday's game, but McCarthy decided to make him inactive, in large part because his conditioning wasn't ready for a game. "My concern for Joey, obviously, is to get him to a spot no different than everybody else in training camp," McCarthy said. "The first players that go through that first ramp-up period that are not ready to go -- they don't participate fully in a padded practice. So I don't really see this any different than that. Now it is different that there's a business component to it, and that's really a whole 'nother topic. "As far as Joey's participation in practice, he's communicating with the trainer every day. He's communicating with the strength and conditioning coach. ... We'll get him out there when he's ready to go through a full practice." McCarthy added that he isn't concerned that Porter's business situation will become a distraction. "Hey, we're preparing to go win our first away game," the coach said. "I think I've answered your questions. Hopefully he gets a step further being ready to play and the business situation will be a business situation. This is the most I've frankly ever talked about a business situation, so I think I'll stop right here." Without Porter, the Steelers almost exclusively used zone coverage. But defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said his scheme varies week to week based on the opponent. Once Porter, who excels in man coverage, returns to the field, Graham's scheme will adapt to include his skill set. And, as Graham pointed out Monday, Porter's traits can also be effective in zone. "Joey's 6-2, 6-3 and long and plays a good length," Graham said. "He can play zone, man; it doesn't matter to me when you watch the tape. He's a good football player. ... Anytime you add new players to what we're going to do, I take that into consideration."

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Jamison Hensley Sep 14, 2026, 04:40 PM ET Close Jamison Hensley is a reporter covering the Baltimore Ravens for ESPN. Jamison joined ESPN in 2011, covering the AFC North before focusing exclusively on the Ravens beginning in 2013. Jamison won the National Sports Media Association Maryland Sportswriter of the Year award in 2018, and he authored a book titled: Flying High: Stories of the Baltimore Ravens. He was the Ravens beat writer for the Baltimore Sun from 2000-2011. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- A day after two of the Baltimore Ravens ' top wide receivers were injured in a 41-23 season-opening win at the Indianapolis Colts , coach Jesse Minter indicated that Zay Flowers is considered day-to-day after aggravating his left hamstring and that Ja'Kobi Lane could be out for a longer period with a wrist injury. Flowers, who is Lamar Jackson 's favorite target, grabbed his left hamstring after being tackled with 5½ minutes left in the first half and didn't play in the second half. After initially being ruled questionable to return, Flowers remained suited up for most of the second half, pacing on the sideline with a slight limp. Before leaving the game, Flowers had totaled 150 yards receiving, the most by a player in the first half in three years. He has proved durable in his four-year career, missing three games. "I feel pretty good about where that's at," Minter said. "We'll see how the week goes though there." Flowers first hurt his hamstring during the joint practices with the Minnesota Vikings on Aug. 20 and sat out for two weeks. He then practiced all last week and was a full participant in Friday's session, which led to him not receiving an injury designation for the season opener. Asked if Flowers has to manage this injury all season, Minter said: "You want to make sure that it's not something you're dealing with for 17, 18 weeks. And so that's all things that as the day-to-day things we'll look at and make sure we're putting Zay in the best position." Lane, a promising rookie third-round pick who is the team's No. 3 wide receiver, injured a wrist in the first half and didn't play after halftime. He finished with one catch for 11 yards but had a 4-yard touchdown in the second quarter negated by a holding penalty. Sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo on Sunday night that the initial diagnosis was Lane fractured the wrist. "We're getting some more things looked at right now and talking to different people," Minter said. Baltimore's only healthy receivers on the 53-man roster are LaJohntay Wester , who has primarily been a punt returner, and Elijah Sarratt , a rookie fourth-round pick who was a healthy scratch in Week 1. The Ravens also have Devontez Walker , who has been dealing with a groin injury, and Chris Moore , who was elevated off the practice squad Sunday and caught a 53-yard pass from Jackson in the fourth quarter. Minter said there is potential to add a free agent wide receiver this week but added that this is an opportunity for Walker and Sarratt to be active Sunday. "I've got a lot of confidence in those guys," Minter said. "Those guys have had a ton of reps within our offense. And then we'll look at all options obviously to figure out what's best."

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play The good and the bad with the Panthers offense (0:47) Mike Kaye Sep 14, 2026, 04:15 PM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales said Sunday after the team's 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears that he needed to watch film before pointing fingers at the problems from the historic defensive downturn. After watching the tape Monday, Canales said the team could have played smarter, noting penalties, poor technique and other mental gaffes. "We played hard," Canales said. "We played with great effort. The guys were together. All those things are true. Playing smart, that's where we fell short. And it was about executing our plan. It was about timely and costly penalties. Certainly, the turnovers ... against a really good team. That's not something that you can do to play the championship football that we need to play." The Bears' offense produced 552 net yards -- Chicago's third-most yardage earned in the Super Bowl era -- with 291 collected on the ground. The 59 points were the most allowed in Panthers' franchise history. The six rushing touchdowns produced by Chicago -- the most in a season opener since 1922, according to ESPN Research -- were shared by three players, including quarterback Caleb Williams , who also threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns for a 124.1 traditional passer rating. "We knew how they were going to attack us," Panthers linebacker Bobby Okereke said. "We practiced a lot of their concepts, and we got a lot of their concepts on game day. And we executed a good bit, but just the run game bit us in the ass today and we gotta be a lot better there." And yet, Canales' main takeaways after watching the film focused on turnovers and penalties. The Panthers' offense and special teams coughed up the ball twice on lost fumbles. Quarterback Bryce Young threw an interception on a pass to wideout Jalen Coker to end the first half, and the offense was stopped while failing to convert on a fourth-down play at the end of the third quarter. But even taking away the 17 points the Bears scored off those mishaps, Chicago still had a five-point advantage over Carolina because of what the defense allowed on the other side. The penalties, though, were inarguably a crux for the Panthers' letdown. Carolina was flagged 11 times for 84 yards, but it was more about the timing of infractions that lost ground. Team captain Derrick Brown was uncharacteristically charged twice -- once for roughing the passer and once for offside -- with the first penalty leading to a touchdown and the second negating an interception by fellow lineman Bobby Brown III and leading to another Bears score. "S--- like that can't happen," Derrick Brown said after the game. Week 1 was the latest in a long line of defensive meltdowns for the Panthers under coordinator Ejiro Evero, who was hired by Carolina in February 2023 under coach Frank Reich. But it was also the biggest one to date, topping a brutal back-to-back stretch to end the 2024 season, when the defense gave up 551 yards to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 17 and 537 yards in the season finale against the Atlanta Falcons . "I like our system," Canales said Monday. "I like our scheme. I've seen this scheme work at a high level, and I've seen us work in this scheme at a high level." "It sucks, but it's one f---ing game," Derrick Brown said Sunday. "We've got a whole season." In 52 regular-season games as the Panthers' defensive coordinator, Evero's unit has given up the highest allowed scoring average in the league at 26.7 points per game, following Sunday's 59-point offering to the Bears. During that span, his group also ranks 26th in the league with a 345.9 yards allowed average per game. The unit also ranks second worst in the league during Evero's tenure in defensive EPA (expected points added) with a minus-250.9 points mark, according to ESPN Research. The defense is also allowing the highest Total QBR in the league (58.3) during that stretch. Following Sunday's loss, the Panthers rank last in points (minus-8.92) and yardage (minus-56) margin averages per game during the Evero era. But it is also worth noting that the offenses, largely anchored by Reich and Canales, have been among the bottom-third of the league throughout Evero's tenure. "I feel like we could just be better as a whole," outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen said about the defense's performance Sunday. "I feel like we could have been more disciplined as a whole unit and just as a whole team in general." During his second season at the helm, Evero's defense was the worst in the league against the run, allowing 179.8 yards per game. The unit also finished last in total yards average, giving up 404.5 yards per game. But last season, the unit improved across the board, ranking 20th in run defense (123.3 rushing yards per game) and 16th overall (327.2 total yards per game). The Panthers added safety Tre'von Moehrig , outside linebacker Patrick Jones II and defensive linemen Bobby Brown III and Tershawn Wharton in free agency during the 2025 offseason. They also selected outside linebackers Umanmielen and Nic Scourton and safety Lathan Ransom in the 2025 draft. This year Carolina continued to beef up its defense, paying a fortune for outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and inside linebacker Devin Lloyd . They drafted defensive tackle Lee Hunter , cornerback Will Lee III, safety Zakee Wheatley and linebacker Jackson Kuwatch as well. Plus, they signed veteran linebacker Bobby Okereke on Aug. 31. The Panthers didn't have Wharton, Jones and Scourton due to injury and Wheatley was a healthy scratch in Week 1. So, while the investment in the defense over the past two years wasn't in full force, the rest of the accumulated talent did little to stop the onslaught of Williams and D'Andre Swift . "Players and coaches alike gotta be better," DT Bobby Brown III said after going through Monday's meetings. "Players didn't execute all the time. Coach [Evero] already told us he didn't get us in the best calls all the time. But when we did have the call right and we felt like we [were] in good positions, everybody didn't show up and make the plays that needed to be made." Canales maintained Monday that the unit has the right talent to turn things around. "And that was one of the things I did share with the team today, I said, 'Look, I wouldn't have been able to sleep if I felt like we didn't have the pieces that we need right in this room.'" Canales said. "And a true statement to those guys. But we need to collectively come together and play way better football than that."

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions AUSTIN, Texas -- After a dramatic 24-23 comeback victory over then-No. 1 Ohio State , Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said Monday that the Buckeyes should be rewarded for playing a marquee matchup in a nonconference game. "I hope Ohio State does not get punished for that game Saturday night. They played a heck of a game. I mean, it's 24-23, they lose to us scoring with 25 seconds to go in the game," Sarkisian said. "I hope if they end up being a 9-3 team, the committee can appreciate the fact that they came to Austin, Texas, in September when it was 100 degrees and played us in that environment and played a heck of a game." Last year, with a College Football Playoff spot on the line late in the season, Sarkisian said he believed the Longhorns shouldn't have been punished for their 14-7 loss to the Buckeyes early in the season. "Ohio State should be rewarded for playing in this game against us," Sarkisian said Monday. "Time will tell. And this isn't crying over spilled milk. I don't think we got rewarded for going to Columbus last year in Week 1. Hopefully, this year they reward Ohio State for coming and playing in this game with us." Ohio State fell to No. 6 in The Associated Press' Top 25 following the loss. Sarkisian reiterated that he does not know how Ohio State's season will unfold and that the conversation will be moot if the Buckeyes go 11-1. He said that he seeks to play in big games and that he knows the Texas "brand" means teams and television networks will want the school in marquee matchups, and he added that he has a locker room full of players who come to Austin to do so. "That's why you come to Texas, to play in these big games," Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning said Monday. "I think it helps our team, builds confidence that we can win in any way. We can be down, we can be not playing well, but we can find ways to win. I think that's what builds confidence in those big games." After his team scored 21 points in the final quarter for the win, Manning sprinted across the field in celebration as the final seconds ticked off. "That was the most fun ending to a game I've ever had," he said. "I did not know what to do. I was just running around." Sarkisian's message was that these heavyweight fights should be considered a strength rather than hurting the teams that lose. "Everybody loves those matchups," Sarkisian said. "Well, if we want to continue with those matchups, we've got to reward the teams for playing in those games ... because if they don't reward them for playing in the game, then all of us start playing FCS, [Group of] 6, and then I don't think that's the product that we want in college football." But the CFP committee makes these games a gamble. "We're not the NFL where it's all based on, 'What's your record? Who did you beat?'" he said. "You make the playoffs based off of opinions of others, essentially, unless you win your conference." After the win, the Longhorns ascended to No. 1 in this week's AP poll, the third season in a row in which Texas has hit that mark. But Sarkisian said the Longhorns are aware that it does not matter two games into the season. "A week ago, the narrative was we can't win the big game," Sarkisian said. "How are we going to beat Ohio State? What are we going to do? Now we're the best team in the country allegedly and everybody's patting us on the back. Two polar opposites of where we are. We need to stay right here, and we need to stay enamored with what we need to do."

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions EAGAN, Minn. -- The hit that caused Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray 's concussion was a "violent, physical play" but was not objectionable, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday. "It would be one thing if there was a headfirst slide and a clear declaration [of giving himself up]," O'Connell said. "But I don't put any fault on anybody there." The injury occurred on the Vikings' 11th offensive snap in Sunday's 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium. At the end of a third-down scramble, Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness and safety Javon Bullard converged on Murray. As the quarterback started going to the ground, contact from Van Ness began to dislodge his helmet. Bullard then hit Murray's head with his right shoulder and forearm. Murray initially was motionless on the turf, and multiple teammates nearby said his body was in a fencing posture, which is a common immediate side effect of brain trauma. Murray eventually walked off the field under his own power. The Vikings placed Murray in the concussion protocol, but he was feeling well enough to chat with teammates and coaches in the postgame locker room. On Monday, O'Connell said that Murray was feeling "pretty good" and did not rule him out of being available for the Vikings' Week 2 game at the Chicago Bears . "He was in meetings today," O'Connell said. "He's not having the type of symptoms where he's not able to be in meetings or things like that. He's able to watch the tape, and we'll just take it a day at a time and see how he's doing and make the determination when that time comes." Carson Wentz , who replaced Murray against the Packers and threw three touchdown passes, would start against the Bears if Murray does not clear the protocol in time. J.J. McCarthy would be the backup. Second-year quarterback Max Brosmer is on the practice squad.

The former Carolina Panthers beat writer for the Charlotte Observer won the APSE award for breaking news and the South Carolina Press Association award for enterprise writing in 2018. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions LAS VEGAS -- Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis might be sore after his first start for his new team. Willis was pressured 17 times in Sunday's 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders , and was sacked five times as the Raiders defense took advantage of obvious passing situations in the second half. He leaves his Dolphins regular season debut tied with Tyler Shough and Deshaun Watson for the most sacks taken in the NFL this week, but he was quick to accept all the blame for what he called a "quarterback stat." "I've got to watch the tape, but you can just blame them all on me," Willis said after the game. "I've got to take care of the ball and I've got to do right by my offensive line and get the ball out and that's everybody. It takes all 11. We got to make sure the receivers are in the right spot, got to make sure I'm doing the right thing. We got to make sure our backs are doing the right thing and it all works together -- but you can blame the sacks on me. "Sacks are a quarterback stat and I'm going to take the O-line out after that." Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 220 yards and an interception Sunday, adding a 14-yard rushing touchdown that proved to be Miami's lone touchdown of the day. Trailing by multiple scores, the Dolphins' offense almost exclusively passed the ball in the second half and Las Vegas' pass rushers pinned their ears back as a result. When facing pressure, Willis completed 5-of-9 passes for 113 yards, notching a 100.5 passer rating with a completion percentage over expectation of 5.9%. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Willis still has his "total confidence and faith," adding that he thought his quarterback made great plays with his legs and arm. But Miami's offense as a whole, he said, was "inconsistent." "Part of the plan to win was to keep the ball moving forward," he said. "I thought the penalties killed us. They forced us into a lot of passing situations that were crucial that you really don't want to be in against that team ... Just like most of the units today, I thought it was inconsistent and that's how we kind of played the game today." Throughout the game, Miami struggled to find easy completions for Willis and he spent an extraordinary amount of time trying to keep plays alive in the backfield in search of an open receiver. Willis finished with an average time to throw of 3.21 seconds, the fourth-longest time of any quarterback in Week 1. He also led the NFL this week with an average air yards per attempt of 13.6 yards, and was off target on 22% of his throws, which was the fourth-highest percentage in the league this week. He did find success when targeting rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas , who finished with a game-high 94 yards on five catches. "I think he's been doing a great job trying to continue to learn and get better," Willis said of Douglas. "He's had a great camp and learned a lot from OTAs and I think he's doing a great job of wanting to get better and wanting to be out there and make plays ... I think (offensive coordinator) Bobby (Slowik) put him in a position to get a couple going and I think it just worked out that way for today." The Dolphins will remain on the west coast, practicing in Northern California this week ahead of their Week 2 game against the San Francisco 49ers (4:25 p.m., E.T., FOX). Both Hafley and Willis said the trip provides a distraction-free opportunity for players to bond and lock into their on-field assignments while they prepare for 49ers defense that held the Los Angeles Rams to 290 yards of offense in Week 1.

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The Bears ' 59-37 victory over the Carolina Panthers in Sunday's early slate kept the momentum of Chicago's offseason hype train going and was representative of a great first Sunday of NFL action for bettors. For starters, the Bears were one of the most popular teams to win and cover the spread (-3) on Sunday, which they did with ease in the second half. DraftKings classified the Bears as the second-most-backed team by bets and handle going into Sunday's action, while BetMGM said Chicago minus-3 was the most-bet spread of the early slate by tickets, with the sportsbook's senior trading manager Christian Cipollini classifying it as "a good outcome for bettors." Then there was the avalanche of touchdowns. Five Bears got in the end zone on Sunday, with QB Caleb Williams and RB D'Andre Swift each getting in multiple times. With the Panthers contributing plenty of scoring on their own, the game flew over its total of 47.5 with 2:35 left in the second quarter. The final score's 96 total points were the most for a Week 1 game in NFL history. The game set the pace for an explosive opening Sunday that saw six teams score 24 or more points in the first half of their games -- also the most in Week 1 in NFL history, according to ESPN research. With players such as Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown , Derrick Henry , Jonathan Taylor and Josh Allen finding the end zone multiple times, that made for a tremendous day for a betting public that makes a habit of rooting for scoring from superstars. "The first NFL Sunday of the season was a champagne-popping day for bettors, while the book was left cleaning up the corks," Caesars Sportsbook football lead Joey Feazel told ESPN. "Seven of the eight morning favorites won outright, six games flew over the total -- many reaching that mark by halftime -- and eight of the top 10 most popular touchdown scorers found the end zone. "Favorites, overs and touchdown scorers combined to create a bettor-friendly trifecta on opening Sunday." Chicago's big win built on the goodwill the team had accrued with bettors throughout the offseason via the futures market -- both for the team as a whole and its star quarterback. The Bears were a hot commodity in a variety of futures markets before the season, chief among them being the Super Bowl. Just before the campaign kicking off, DraftKings reported 7.5% of its Super Bowl handle backing Chicago -- the third most behind the Los Angeles Rams (20.2%) and Buffalo Bills (9.8%) -- while BetMGM said the Bears had garnered the most NFC championship tickets at 14.4%. Feazel called Chicago "a moderate position" in the Super Bowl market Sunday. "Chicago's offense looks great," Circa Sports NFL oddsmaker Jamey Pileggi told ESPN. "Bad defense is going to hold them back from being real contenders." At DraftKings, Chicago made only a small move from 24-1 to 21-1 to win the title, but the big odds move came for Williams in the MVP market, where he went from 12-1 to +700, tying him for second with Lamar Jackson behind Allen in the lead at +500. Several sportsbooks considered Williams a liability in the awards market coming into the season, and he accumulated around 10% of the tickets at both BetMGM and Caesars. Joe Burrow (+950) has been the public's favorite throughout the offseason, but if Williams can continue to put up performances like Sunday's, he could continue to gain traction with bettors. "Given his Week 1 performance and the amount of early support we've already seen, we would expect Caleb Williams to remain one of the more heavily backed players in the MVP market moving forward," Feazel said. Odds & Ends The Arizona Cardinals closed as 8.5-point underdogs to the Los Angeles Chargers before upsetting them outright on the road. It was the largest Week 1 upset since 2018 ( Tampa Bay Buccaneers +10 over the New Orleans Saints ). The Chargers were the most-picked team in ESPN Survivor contests (21.4%), the second-most in Circa Survivor (30.3%) and the second-most in Splash Sports' $1,000 entry survivor contest (21.5%). The Cardinals are the first team with a preseason win total of 3.5 or lower to win their Week 1 game since at least 1990, according to ESPN Research. After losing and failing to cover plus-3.5 on Sunday, the Buccaneers are now 0-10 against the spread in their past 10 games, tying the longest ATS losing streak in the Super Bowl era. On the flip side, the Jacksonville Jaguars have covered nine consecutive regular-season games, the longest ATS winning streak since the Green Bay Packers in 2021 and the longest in Jaguars history. ESPN's David Purdum contributed to this report.

He joined ESPN in 2015, writes regularly for ESPN+ and spent multiple years on "NFL Matchup." After graduating from the University of Iowa, Matt played safety in the NFL for St. Louis, Green Bay, Washington and Buffalo over seven seasons. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Week 1 wraps up with Patrick Mahomes making his return to action when the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football" ( 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC ). I love Week 1 games with divisional opponents because it gives us a road map of what to look for based on previous head-to-head matchups, which includes personnel usage, scheme and more. And we get that here with Denver and K.C. on Monday night. Yes, there is an unknown in this game with Mahomes after the season-ending knee injury in 2025. He's a natural mover and creator. Let's keep an eye on his mobility in this one. Now, going back to the Week 11 Broncos-Chiefs game last season (when Mahomes was on the field), Denver lowered their blitz rate slightly to 28.6% (down from their season average of 31.3%). And what do you get from the Denver secondary? A lot of single-high looks and man coverage. Mahomes attempted 45 passes in that game, threw for 267 yards and was sacked three times. My take for Monday? Coach Andy Reid will use the run game -- and free agent addition Kenneth Walker III -- to control tempo out of multiple tight end sets. You don't want Mahomes dropping back 40-plus times versus this Denver pass rush. On the offensive side for the Broncos, Davis Webb takes over as the new playcaller, though I expect to see coach Sean Payton's influence in the game plan, which includes the quicks and shot plays deigned for offseason addition Jaylen Waddle . Waddle fits the Denver route tree and the throwing traits of Bo Nix . The key here is Nix's ability to reads the heavy post-snap movement from Chiefs defense. In the backfield, we should look for a committee approach with J.K. Dobbins , RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman versus a top-10 Kansas City run front. Betting outlook Do we feel that Mahomes is back to a point where he can take over critical moments of the game by extending plays outside of structure? Or does Reid have to craft a game plan that leans on running the ball and throwing quick from the pocket to counter a Denver pass rush that had an NFL-best 68 sacks last season? I think it's a little of both, even if Mahomes is somewhat limited as a runner. Playing in Arrowhead helps here for Kansas City. That's the toughest road environment I ever experienced as a player (though Philly is close). The spread dipping under the three-point mark works, too. And when I look at Week 1 games, the value of coaching really jumps. We saw that in the 49ers-Rams game, right? And Reid has had an entire offseason to study a very multiple (and pressure-heavy) Denver defense. If Steve Spagnulo's defense can limit the after-the-catch production versus Denver (gotta tackle), while creating a few takeaways, this sets up a physical, low-scoring Chiefs' winner. The bets: Chiefs -2.5 (-105), Walker receiving yards OVER 17.5 (-116) Notable player props, bets Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Bo Nix rushing yards OVER 16.5 (-108) Eric Moody: Nix has averaged 23.1 rushing yards per game in his career. With the Chiefs allowing the 10th-fewest passing yards per game last season, Nix could rely more on his legs in this matchup. He cleared this line in 10 of 18 games last season, and even though he's returning from a broken ankle that kept him out of the AFC championship, there's a strong chance he clears this line on Monday night. Travis Kelce receiving yards OVER 41.5 (-112) Liz Loza: Kelce registered 42 or more receiving yards in 13 of 18 regular-season contests last season. Moreover, he has managed 43 or more receiving yards in five of his last six meetings against Denver. The Broncos' defense allowed an average of nearly 60 receiving yards per game to tight ends in 2025 (ninth most). With Mahomes working his way back into game shape, Kelce figures to serve as a reliable safety valve on primetime.

Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images ESPN Multiple Authors Sep 14, 2026, 10:48 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions With most of Week 1 of the NFL season in the books, we're already looking ahead to Week 2 . The Buffalo Bills will debut their new stadium Thursday night against the Detroit Lions in a game that has the highest total of the young season (53.5). The biggest spread of the week belongs to the San Francisco 49ers , who will host the Miami Dolphins . Of course, Week 1's biggest favorite, the Los Angeles Chargers , lost outright to the Arizona Cardinals . Matt Bowen, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody and Seth Walder looked at the early Week 2 odds and identified which ones are worth jumping on now before potential shifts later in the week. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Carolina Panthers +1.5 at Atlanta Falcons Matt Bowen: It's a bounce-back game for a Panthers team that showed explosive-play juice versus the Chicago Bears in Week 1. Bryce Young threw for 361 yards, and we saw the perimeter one-on-one ability of Jalen Coker . Sure, the Carolina defense gave up 59 points. That's bad football. But the Atlanta quarterback situation (due to injuries) limits that offense. Let's take Carolina to cover on the road. Seattle Seahawks at Cardinals total points UNDER 41.5 Pamela Maldonado: The Cardinals controlled Week 1, but they did so through short passes, long drives and 34 rushing attempts that produced 3.4 yards per carry. Seattle's offense went 2-of-11 on third down and failed to score a touchdown on either red zone trip. Both defenses also forced turnovers and limited explosive opportunities. Unless those red zone results swing drastically, this should be another slow divisional game heavy on field goals. Lions at Bills total points OVER 53.5 Eric Moody: The over is appealing after both teams opened the season in high-scoring affairs. Detroit's game totaled 61 points, while Buffalo's reached 67. The Lions just gave up 410 passing yards and three touchdowns to Tyler Shough , and now they get Josh Allen , who accounted for four touchdowns against the Houston Texans . Buffalo's defense also allowed 31 points and 381 yards. Both offenses can score in bunches, and neither defense looked especially dominant in Week 1. New England Patriots -5.5 vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Seth Walder: The Patriots' offense was stymied in Week 1 and lost A.J. Brown for at least four games due to his high ankle sprain. Not ideal! But I think anyone can be forgiven for failing to score on the Seahawks' defense. And the Patriots were uncharacteristically run-heavy on first down in that game. This was an outrageously efficient pass-first team last year without Brown. It can be that again. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh struggled to pull away from the Cooper Rush -led Falcons. That's far more bearish than a loss to the reigning champs.

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics play Myles Garrett recounts 'shock and joy' of being traded to Rams (1:26) Sarah Barshop Sep 14, 2026, 10:35 AM ET Close Sarah Barshop covers the Los Angeles Rams for ESPN. She joined ESPN in 2016 to cover the Green Bay Packers for ESPN Milwaukee. She then moved to Houston to cover the Texans. She came to ESPN after working as a writer and editor for Sports Illustrated. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald , who un-retired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7 all-time. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach top-five all-time territory. Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him. But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks were 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research, heading into the seaosn. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the all-time list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White. As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. Week 1 update Of all of the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee. After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Andres Waters Sep 14, 2026, 09:11 AM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The NFL season has just begun, but players and even coaches have been in midseason form after their opening games, providing plenty of interesting moments during postgame speeches in the locker room, interviews at the podium and on social media. Ahead of the first "Monday Night Football" matchup of the year between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos , we rounded up the best quotes from around the league on Sunday. "He had 124 [yards] on the ground, three touchdowns and a brand-new f---ing contract." -- Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson The Bears coach was fired up for his team in the locker room after beating the Carolina Panthers in a 59-37 shootout. While handing out game balls to his players, Johnson made sure to mention star running back D'Andre Swift 's recent massive payday. It was reported two days ago that Swift and Chicago had agreed to a three-year, $33.75 million extension . What you've all been waiting for ‼️ pic.twitter.com/TokagQtpMB Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) September 13, 2026 "I'm Malaki Starks, and I'm a dawg." -- Baltimore Ravens DB Malaki Starks During his usual postgame stream on social media with teammates following a victory, defensive back Marlon Humphrey caught up with Starks. The Ravens throttled the Indianapolis Colts 41-23 , posting over 500 total yards of offense. While Starks was giving an honest breakdown of his team's performance on Sunday afternoon, Humphrey was having none of that. Instead, Humphrey told the sophomore safety to let the world know just how talented he is. . @starks_malaki certified DAWG Via @marlon_humphrey IG live pic.twitter.com/X6HhtDFpHt Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) September 13, 2026 "Plain and simple, we got our ass whupped." -- Colts DT DeForest Buckner While it was all smiles and laughs for the Ravens on Sunday, their opponent's locker room was anything but. Indianapolis allowed 506 total yards and gave up 41 points, its second-most points allowed in a season opener in the past 10 seasons, according to ESPN Research. When asked about his team's performance in its home opener, Buckner didn't hold back. "I guess I've got to get 200 [touchdown passes] now. I'll keep that one." -- Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence Lawrence threw for four touchdowns in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns , but one of them was more special than the rest. His second TD toss to rookie receiver Josh Cameron was the 100th of his career. However, it was also Cameron's first career NFL catch. Knowing this was a special moment for the rookie pass catcher, Lawrence graciously let Cameron keep the ball. But he won't be so generous with the one from his 200th touchdown pass. "Waited a long time to be a head coach in this league, man. It's freaking awesome. And we're not where we want to be, and they better get us now." -- Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken The first-year head coach expressed his disappointment following a defeat to the Jaguars. However, Monken offered some optimism for the future, too. He focused on his young group improving, while pinpointing that they just "didn't play well today." Monken spent 10 seasons as an assistant coach in the NFL before getting his first head coaching job. Therefore, the blowout loss presumably won't get him too shook up, as he added: "You're not going to get me down." Todd Monken on the Browns' blowout loss in his first game as an NFL head coach: I'm not down. I'm disappointed. I mean, you're not going to get me down. Waited a long time to be a head coach in this league, man. It's freaking awesome. And we're not where we want to be, and they... Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 13, 2026 "There's a time and place for everything." -- Washington Commanders QB Jayden Daniels Washington suffered a narrow two-point defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles following a failed 2-point conversation late. One play that might have had an impact on the outcome happened early in the fourth quarter. Daniels connected with wide receiver Stefon Diggs for a 10-yard touchdown to make it a one-point game. However, Diggs celebrated by leaping on the goalpost and received a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty. It pushed the Commanders' PAT back, though the kick was good anyway. After the game, coach Dan Quinn said the team would have gone for two if Diggs wasn't penalized. Washington's quarterback reflected on Diggs' penalty postgame. There's a time and place for everything. -Jayden Daniels on Stefon Diggs getting a penalty for celebrating in the Commanders' Week 1 loss to the Eagles. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/UYTaQtRkPv ESPN (@espn) September 14, 2026
