Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Brooke Pryor Sep 13, 2026, 06:44 PM ET Close Brooke Pryor is a reporter for NFL Nation at ESPN who has covered the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. She previously covered the Kansas City Chiefs for the Kansas City Star and the University of Oklahoma for The Oklahoman. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions PITTSBURGH -- Clutching a worn football, Mike McCarthy walked from locker to locker late Sunday afternoon, checking in with his players as music celebrating the Pittsburgh Steelers ' season-opening 20-13 win against the Atlanta Falcons bumped from the corner of the locker room. McCarthy grinned as he chatted briefly with linebacker Patrick Queen . After a few moments, he pivoted and strode across the room toward the hallways that led to the postgame press conference room. On his way, he bumped into T.J. Watt , and the jolly head coach jokingly jostled his star pass rusher, still securely holding the football tucked under his arm. By the time McCarthy took his place on the dais for his news conference, the football was safely stowed away. Because of all the game balls he has received, this one, given to him by quarterback Aaron Rodgers after McCarthy's first win as the Pittsburgh Steelers' head coach, has a little extra meaning. "Mike's had a lot of wins, but it's always special when it's the first one at a place, and extra special when it's the team you grew up cheering for and you grew up just on the other side of the river from the facility," said Rodgers, who spent 13 seasons with McCarthy in Green Bay. "[His] parents are still living in town, so super special to be able to do that. I was really honestly looking forward to that today as much as anything." McCarthy, his voice catching ever so slightly, expressed gratitude for the gesture, but he also quickly tried to turn the attention to his team's efforts. "First team ball, first win," he said. "So it's obviously a special moment. I really appreciate the guys. Appreciate Aaron and the kind words, and it's time to move on to get team victories from here on. I'm not one for attention. So, the homecoming's been great. I'm just glad to get this one under our belt." The Steelers were able to get that win under their belts in large part thanks to a dominant performance by the their pass rush. Led by Watt's two sacks and a pick-six, the Steelers sacked third-string quarterback Cooper Rush four times and recorded five quarterback hits. And in the secondary, Pittsburgh native and free agency acquisition Jaquan Brisker recorded a first-half interception in his first game as a Steeler. Reinvigorated in the new defensive scheme under coordinator Patrick Graham, Watt sealed the win early in the fourth quarter when he leaped near the line of scrimmage and plucked Rush's ball out of the air. He tumbled untouched to the turf a few steps after. Then, a voice urged him to get up and keep going. Watt jumped up and finished the play, sprinting 35 yards to the end zone for the score. "I think it was Nu [ Keeanu Benton ] that was like, 'Get up, get up,' because I had no idea where I was," Watt said. "I had no bearing at all. I'm sure the fall didn't look too graceful, but glad someone told me to get up and keep running." That Watt was in a position to make that play was a byproduct of Graham's emphasis on rotating his defensive front to keep everyone as fresh as possible. Watt and Nick Herbig each played 37 defensive snaps, while Alex Highsmith , who had two sacks, played 40, and second-year pass rusher Jack Sawyer played 21. "The rotation that we have, as you guys saw, and getting less reps but trying to exert as much as you possibly can on those reps, making them mean that much more," Watt said. "Give a lot of credit to [outside linebacker coach] C.J. [Ah You] for keeping track of it. Helped us play and be more fresh today." With his interception, Watt joined Julius Peppers as the only players in NFL history with 10 interceptions and 100 sacks. The play also marked his second career defensive touchdown and first career interception return. Watt celebrated by doing Deion Sanders' Primetime celebration into the end zone, high-stepping his way across the goal line with his hands up. "I think it was just the first thing that always pops in my head," Watt said with a laugh. "I don't know why I do it, but I think it looks cool." The Steelers needed the game-sealing score from Watt in part because after not playing together in the preseason, the starting offense was a little clunky. Rodgers completed 24 of 40 attempts for 221 yards with a touchdown and two sacks, but the Steelers' downfield attack was inconsistent with several incompletions and drops by DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson . Earlier in the game, Rodgers seemingly manifested Watt's big play as the quarterback chatted with fellow signal caller Mason Rudolph on the sideline. "We just said, 'Hey, it'd be awesome if we got a couple special teams or defensive scores this year,'" Rodgers said. "And then we were talking about T.J. right before he got to pick-six. We got to figure out what the juju and mojo energy is with that. It's a big deal. It's a game changer for sure." Whatever it was, it helped seal a storybook debut for McCarthy -- and the last first game of Rodgers' career. Like his coach, though, Rodgers is trying not to focus on those individual milestones. "Not until right now," Rodgers said, asked if he had reflected on it being his last season opener. "So thank you for that. But I'm very happy to be 1-0, and happy to get that first win off of Mike's checklist and move on. Get ready for next week in New England."

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Judy Battista Multiple Authors Sep 13, 2026, 06:42 PM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions HOUSTON -- Josh Allen was still sweating when he got to the microphone and uttered something that would have been inconceivable just a year ago: "We do like Reliant Stadium!" For good reason. In a house of Bills horrors -- they hadn't won here since 2006 -- against a team that battered him last season, Allen produced a whopper of an offensive performance as Buffalo outlasted the Houston Texans 36-31 on Sunday, giving Joe Brady his first victory as coach. The Bills ran just 52 plays but totaled 409 yards of offense, an average of 7.9 yards per play. Twice, they started drives at their own 4-yard line and finished with touchdowns. A big part of the efficiency was a more downfield passing attack. Allen completed 11 of 15 throws that traveled at least 10 yards in the air for 286 yards and two touchdowns, including a 34-yarder that he rifled down the deep middle of the field to Joshua Palmer for the winning score. Asked how he felt about all the big plays, Allen was succinct. "Hell, yeah," he said. "We love chunk plays. That's how you score 36 points. You give yourself opportunities to score in four, five plays in a drive instead of long, methodical, 13, 14, 15 plays. That's also a way to win football games." Allen, who also rushed for two touchdowns, has a career 303 TDs, making him the first player in NFL history to reach 300 in his first nine seasons. He is also 20th on the all-time rushing touchdowns list, tied with Frank Gore and Ottis Anderson and one behind Corey Dillon. It was Allen's ninth career game with two passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns, five more than any other player in NFL history. Steve Young had four. Since he entered the league in 2018, Allen has had 18 games in which he has rushed for two or more TDs. Aside from the sheer volume of yards per play, the most glaring difference for Allen and the Bills was that Allen was upright. Last November, the Texans sacked Allen eight times. On Sunday, he was sacked just twice and was barely pressured in the first half. The Bills committed to chipping the Texans, and Buffalo used three tight ends on 40.4% of its plays. The result was that Allen had plenty of time in the pocket, completing passes to seven different pass catchers. D.J. Moore (5 catches, 100 yards, 1 touchdown) and Dalton Kincaid (5 catches, 130 yards) eclipsed the 100-yard mark, the first time the Bills had multiple players have at least 100 yards receiving in a game since Week 5 of the 2023 season. "We were trying to limit their D-line from wrecking this game," Allen said. "When you're able to sit back in the pocket against a team like this, with two edges like this, you feel pretty good when your guys can hold up, and we did tonight." "Sometimes, all you need is another half-second." Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said his club's defense has "to make plays. It's simple as that. We had opportunities to make plays and we didn't make plays." Kincaid said doubting Allen is "odd," and certainly there is no doubt among the Bills, who were jubilant in the locker room. "When we're at full strength, it's hard to beat us," Kincaid said. Allen said throughout the game that it never seemed like it was Brady's first as a head coach. As the Bills were driving for what would be the winning score, Brady was fully in his element. He was elevated from offensive coordinator to replace Sean McDermott because the Bills needed someone to get them over the hump and win a Super Bowl. Joe Brady: Man of the people. pic.twitter.com/uPvXSgW0NX Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) September 13, 2026 The margin for what will be considered a success is slim for Brady. Game 1 was a good start, though. "I live for those moments," he said. "I coach for those critical moments. I expect our guys to be at their best. I have to be at my best. Seeing Josh, 'Hey, look, I'm taking a shot.' Josh Palmer, trusted. That's who we have to be. Making sure they have to play us and not the other way around." Next up are the Detroit Lions on Thursday night as the Bills open their new stadium. New stadium, new season, same Josh Allen. ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime contributed to this report.

Prior to ESPN, he covered the Miami Dolphins for the Miami Herald, as well as the Baltimore Ravens for The Baltimore Sun. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Todd Monken sidestepped a question about whether he will stick with Deshaun Watson as his starter after a 34-10 Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, but the Cleveland Browns ' coach emphasized the team's struggles on offense didn't only lie with the veteran quarterback. Watson struggled through the first three quarters, completing 11 of 17 passes for 100 yards with an interception as Cleveland watched Jacksonville take a 34-3 lead. He finished 16-of-22 for 205 yards with a touchdown, an interception and 38 rushing yards. "I'd rather just talk about today, because I haven't had time to even look at the tape," Monken said. "I'm sure as hell not firing me. I'm not firing our staff. I'm not getting rid of all of our players. So he happens to be one of 53, and however many practice squad guys we got and our staff, he's one of them. So we'll evaluate everything. But to just say that emotionally here at the end -- when we didn't play good enough and didn't coach well enough." The Browns trailed 24-0 at halftime, tying their worst halftime shutout in the past 35 years, according to ESPN Research. Through two quarters, Cleveland had only five first downs on six drives and were 0-for-4 on third down. Watson completed his first two passes on the Browns' opening possession as Cleveland's offense traveled into Jacksonville territory, but his third attempt was intercepted by linebacker Foye Oluokun . The Browns failed to build momentum after the giveaway, as they punted on the next two possessions, lost the ball on a fumble by rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion and punted again before the end of the first half. The Jaguars, meanwhile, scored on their first four possessions of the first half. "I think we just got to find a rhythm overall," Watson said. "Of course everyone's going to look at the quarterback in the situation. ... We got to put points on the board, and that's what you got to do in this league. Playing the quarterback position, you're the leader in that role. And we didn't do that today. We only got 10. We left a lot out there. So obviously I take that responsibility full throttle, and we got to look at the tape and see how we can be better and try to attack Tampa Bay next week to be able to get points on the board to be able to get wins." The pre-snap operation, a point of emphasis for Monken, was also an issue in Jacksonville. Cleveland was flagged for six accepted penalties on offense, including two delay-of-game infractions. "It wasn't all him," Monken said. "It really wasn't all him. That's unfair. Certainly could have called it better, certainly could have played better around him. Certainly there's plays I'm sure he wished he had back. There are certain things operationally that weren't clean enough. Us getting in and out of the huddle, getting our subs in, being up against it and saying that you're on the road or the heat or all that, that's just a bunch of excuses." Watson, who turns 31 on Monday, was playing his first regular-season game in 693 days. Monken named him the team's starting quarterback on Aug. 24 after a training camp competition with Shedeur Sanders -- two days after Watson struggled in the second half of a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills and then called Browns fans who booed him disrespectful. "We'll analyze everything that we do," Monken said. "It's not just him. We're putting this on Deshaun, which is unfair. And whatever there is externally doesn't matter to me. That doesn't affect me. That has nothing to do with my decision-making. My decision-making is what's best for the Browns now and moving forward. That doesn't mean that I don't understand the frustration. I've said that since I've been here. Same with me. I didn't take this job to lose."

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Turron Davenport Sep 13, 2026, 06:03 PM ET Close Turron Davenport covers the Tennessee Titans for ESPN since 2018. Turron is a former collegiate football player at Cheyney University and is a native of Philadelphia, and he has authored/co-authored four books. You can catch Turron on ESPN Radio on his show "Talking with TD." Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Coach Robert Saleh's Tennessee Titans ' debut did not go anywhere near how he planned. The Titans suffered a 23-10 loss to Saleh's former team, the New York Jets , while quarterback Cam Ward had a tough outing, completing 19 of 32 attempts for 140 yards and one touchdown. Ward's accuracy issues carried over from last year to Sunday. Ward missed easy throws near the line of scrimmage to running back Tyjae Spears and wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson . Ward also missed what would have been a big play to Carnell Tate across the middle on third-and-3 in the second quarter. Ward acknowledged he missed some easy throws. "Those are some big plays that we could have had, but we still got a lot of things to clean up for sure," Ward said. "I'm very disappointed. We're better than what we showed offensively. We trained a lot this offseason. We had some hard days. It didn't pay off for us today, but it's going to pay off for us eventually, whether it's next week or the week after, but we're going to get it rolling, and it's exciting." Saleh hiring Brian Daboll as offensive coordinator this offseason to work with Ward drew a lot of excitement. But the Titans' offense scored only one touchdown in six drives during the preseason and didn't reach the end zone Sunday until late in the fourth quarter, when Ward found Elic Ayomanor on a slant for an 11-yard touchdown with the game already out of reach. The frustration mounted as fans began to boo, especially during the four three-and-outs resulting in punts. Saleh heard the boos but vowed not to make any rash decisions after a frustrating loss to a team that finished equally as bad as the Titans at 3-14 last season. "I think everyone's a little frustrated," Saleh said. "Don't confuse my calm demeanor with frustration, but before I blurt and start screaming, I'm going to watch tape and try to make sure that we make rational, educated football decisions to make sure that we're putting our players in the best position to be successful. Same thing with our players. I can throw podiums around if you want to make everyone feel good. But it's really go back, watch the tape, figure it out and see if we can get better from this." Added Ward, "It doesn't make me feel any type of way. The fans come here for a show. They spend their money to come see the Titans win games, and we want them out here each and every day."

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Anthony Gharib Sep 13, 2026, 11:49 PM ET Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions It's just Week 1 of the NFL season, but that doesn't mean the trolls are starting out slow. The New York Giants defeated the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on "Sunday Night Football." New York enjoyed a wire-to-wire win behind a stellar performance from quarterback Jaxson Dart . He had 230 passing yards and three passing touchdowns, plus 54 yards rushing. Dart is the third quarterback in Giants history with three passing touchdowns and 50 rushing yards in a game, according to ESPN Research. New York's defense had a say in the victory, too, holding Dallas to just 244 total yards of offense -- the fewest for the Cowboys versus the Giants since 2008. In his debut with the team, Giants tight end Isaiah Likely had eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns. New York's win didn't come without a petty post on social media aimed at its rivals. The Giants shared a video of "SpongeBob SquarePants" character Sandy Cheeks, who is from Texas, playing "Sandy's Texas Song." The track ends with Sandy going down into her tree dome while singing the lyrics: "I want to go home." In this case, it's presumably the Cowboys who want to go home. View this post on Instagram A post shared by New York Giants (@nygiants) Here are more of the top trolls from Week 1 of the NFL season. Buffalo Bills 36, Houston Texans 31 In an early-season matchup between two AFC favorites, the Buffalo Bills defeated the Houston Texans on Sunday. The high-scoring affair came to an end when Buffalo linebacker Greg Rousseau had a sack fumble on Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud with 16 seconds left in the game. Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen had 334 passing yards and four total touchdowns -- two on the ground and two in the air. Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid led the team with 130 receiving yards, while wide receiver DJ Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two scores. The big victory came with simple trolls from Buffalo. First, it posted an image of someone doing a horns down motion to the Texans' mascot, Toro. Then, the Bills put a spin on the city of Houston's famous blue tiles, creating their own sign that read: "Bills Win," with the Houston skyline in the background. Horns down. pic.twitter.com/m1sivsnhf3 Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) September 13, 2026 H-Town W. 😄 pic.twitter.com/o6IkBUMH0l Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) September 13, 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers 20, Atlanta Falcons 13 The first game of the Mike McCarthy era in Pittsburgh began with a W as the Steelers defeated the Falcons at home. Pittsburgh's defense showed out with two forced turnovers, including a pick-six by linebacker T.J. Watt , and four sacks. Watt had two of those sacks, becoming the first Steelers player with at least two sacks and an interception return for a touchdown in a game since LaMarr Woodley in 2010, according to ESPN Research. The victory came with a postgame jab aimed at the Falcons' namesake. Pittsburgh posted a viral TikTok audio and meme with a bird hopping up and down when exiting a cage with the caption: "Feather in our cap." Feather in our cap pic.twitter.com/tXMIQG03ys Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) September 13, 2026 San Francisco 49ers 27, Los Angeles Rams 7 Even from down under, the trolls hit the same. San Francisco made sure to poke fun at its division rival after a dominant win in Australia. The 49ers' statement victory against the Rams on Thursday night included 24 unanswered points to close it out. Los Angeles had just 290 offensive yards plus two turnovers, while San Francisco hummed all game. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy threw for 205 passing yards and three touchdowns to three different players -- wide receivers Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel Sr. and Demarcus Robinson . While in Australia, San Francisco seemingly picked up on trends of the Oceanic country. One of them became the theme of its troll: Vegemite, a thick Australian spread made from brewer's yeast . It has a strong, salty and meaty-rich flavor, according to Food Network . The 49ers spread it out on a piece of bread to spell out "W," presumably served up for the Rams. The best kind of spread 🍽️ pic.twitter.com/4pYe2cfMv6 San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 11, 2026 Seattle Seahawks 13, New England Patriots 10 Seattle's championship-defending season began with a victory against New England last Wednesday. The Seahawks lost quarterback Sam Darnold on the first drive due to a hip injury. Drew Lock stepped up under center and threw for 187 yards and a touchdown. However, Seattle's defense made the plays of the game, picking off Patriots quarterback Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to help secure the win. No different from last season, a Seahawks victory came with a comic trolling of the other team, this time the Patriots. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Seattle Seahawks (@seahawks)

Arizona Cardinals 2d ESPN staff NFL win rate metrics leaderboard: Ranking the best in pass rushing, run stopping and blocking 2d ESPN Analytics Kevin Seifert Sep 13, 2026, 05:14 PM ET Close Kevin Seifert is a staff writer who covers the Minnesota Vikings and the NFL at ESPN. Kevin has covered the NFL for over 20 years, joining ESPN in 2008. He was previously a beat reporter for the Minneapolis Star Tribune and Washington Times. He is a graduate of the University of Virginia. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions EAGAN, Minn. -- Quarterback Kyler Murray was chatting with teammates and coaches in the Minnesota Vikings ' victorious postgame locker room Sunday, hours after a hit to his head left him motionless on the field at U.S. Bank Stadium. Multiple players confirmed that Murray's body was in a fencing posture, a common but scary immediate reaction to brain trauma, and the Vikings' medical staff diagnosed him with a concussion. Murray was unavailable for comment after being put in the NFL's concussion protocol, but coach Kevin O'Connell was among those who were encouraged by his disposition in the locker room after the Vikings' 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers . "I don't have a lot to update," O'Connell said, "other than I did just see him and he seemed to be doing pretty well." Backup Carson Wentz , named the No. 2 quarterback last week, replaced Murray and threw three touchdown passes. Wentz will be the starter until Murray returns, with J.J. McCarthy as the likely backup and possibly Max Brosmer -- currently on the practice squad -- at No. 3. The Vikings' next game is Sunday at the Chicago Bears . Murray, who won the Vikings' starting job this summer after signing a one-year contract in March, suffered the concussion on the 11th play of his regular-season debut in Minnesota. He had thrown an interception on his first pass before completing three of his next four for 18 yards. Then, on a third-and-6 with 6 minutes, 16 seconds left in the first quarter, he began scrambling. Murray slid at the Vikings' 35-yard line as Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness and safety Javon Bullard converged. Van Ness' hit pulled Murray's helmet while Bullard hit him with his right shoulder. Referee Shawn Hochuli's crew penalized Bullard for unnecessary roughness. Right tackle Brian O'Neill was one of the first players to arrive. O'Neill shoved Bullard and said he regretted not doing more in retaliation. "It was so bang, bang," O'Neill said. "You don't want to freak out if you're wrong. I was probably wrong to not freak out more than that. So I kind of wish I took a shot at him." Said receiver Justin Jefferson : "Obviously somebody hit him while he was down. But as soon as that happened and I saw his reaction to that, it was really just frustration. I hate to see anyone go down with an injury, especially an injury like that. For our starting quarterback to go down that early in that way, it was definitely very tough to see." Running back Aaron Jones Sr . was watching from the Vikings' sideline but acknowledged he was alarmed. "It almost puts me in a bad head space in a way because you never want to see anybody get hit like that," Jones said. "And then especially to me, when somebody's posturing on the field, that's when it's scary. We know what we sign up for, but at the same time you never want to see that happen and you hope that it's never one of your teammates or you. "So we're praying for him, and it takes something from you a little bit and man, it brings you back to reality." The Vikings trailed 3-0 at the time, but the Packers scored on their next two possessions and ultimately held a 19-10 lead at halftime. Wentz appeared a bit rusty after taking only a handful of reps in training camp, and none in practice with the starting offense since he was named the No. 2 quarterback. But Wentz settled in to complete six of his final seven passes, including two of his touchdowns. Overall, Wentz completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards. In the process, he became the third NFL backup since at least 1950 to throw three touchdowns and no interceptions in his team's season opener, a testament to how rare of a position he was thrust into Sunday. "It was a different process [this summer], I'm not going to lie," Wentz said. "But I've stayed as ready as I could. Mental reps, reps after practice, whatever that looks like, and at the end of the day leaving it in God's hands. I'm confident in what I bring to the table, what I can do and if my number gets called and that I can step up when needed. "So who knew how it was going to play out? None of us did in here, but I trusted God through it. Football is a funny game."

Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The first NFL Week has arrived, and with it comes fresh fits around the league. In recent years, NFL players' arrival outfits have become more sophisticated and diverse. Sometimes, they are suited and booted. Other times it's simply trendy streetwear. "It's like I put on a costume," Dallas Cowboys linebacker Von Miller told ESPN. "It gives me a different energy, a different spark." Miller isn't the only player who believes a great fit can set the tone before a game. "When I put on a fire fit, I tell myself it's time to turn up. Gunners make an impact: Darius Cooper, Tyler Owens, Tay Martin and Khalil Dorsey each recorded two tackles without a miss while aligned as gunners. Introducing the NEW PFF Pro subscription : PFF Pro includes everything in PFF+, plus an upgraded Premium Stats Pro experience, higher base access to Guru AI, revamped player and team pages, enhanced data and visualizations, an improved interface and programmatic data access for modeling. Click here to subscribe. Each week through the 2026 NFL season, I'll be taking a closer look at the special teams players making an impact around the NFL. But this won’t just be about the kickers, punters and returners who typically get the attention. We’ll dig deeper into the players who can decide games without touching the ball, from gunners and vices to snappers and members of the kick return and coverage units. I’ll also highlight my favorite special teams plays of the week. Here is the Special Teams Report for Week 1. Special teams play of the week The play design for the Arizona Cardinals ’ blocked punt against the Los Angeles Chargers was excellent. As soon as the long snapper put his head down to prepare to snap the ball, the Cardinals shifted linebacker Cody Simon from one side of the formation to the other. After the snap, Simi Fehoko stunted over a gap. The result was an overload, leaving the Chargers with too many players to block. Fehoko was left unblocked and got to the ball as it left the punter’s foot. Cardinals blocked punt yesterday was awesome. Shift Cody Simon late (as soon as the long snapper's head goes down) then stunt Semi Fehoko who gets the block 👏 pic.twitter.com/I21Jd3cQ0V Gordon McGuinness (@GordonNFL) September 14, 2026 Gunners Darius Cooper of the Philadelphia Eagles , Tyler Owens of the Washington Commanders , and Tay Martin and Khalil Dorsey of the Detroit Lions each recorded two tackles without a missed tackle when lined up as gunners. No rep was more impressive than Owens', who went viral after beating two blockers, knocking them both to the ground, before making the tackle. Tyler Owens could not be stopped 😳 WASvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d4Tyw1MnqS NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Vise/Jammers On the other side are the players responsible for trying to slow down gunners. Four players who were on the field for three or more snaps as a vise/jammer recorded a 33.3% vise win rate, tied for the league lead: Kamal Hadden of the Green Bay Packers, Chris Blair of the Atlanta Falcons, Jordan Howden of the New Orleans Saints and Christian Braswell of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Howden’s successful block for the Saints helped spark a 16-yard punt return. Long snappers Long snappers earn high PFF grades by limiting bad snaps and by recording tackles in punt coverage. Six long snappers earned PFF grades above 80.0 in Week 1. Tucker Addington of the Miami Dolphins led the league at 90.6, with no negatively graded snaps and a pair of tackles.
